`Buffer` trait定义了如何将缓冲区传递给底层系统调用，并处理读取的字节数。它支持多种类型，包括`&mut [u8]`和`&mut [MaybeUninit<T>]`，后者允许读取到未初始化的缓冲区。此外，`Buffer`还支持通过`Vec`的备用容量进行读取，避免动态分配。

使用示例展示了如何用`Buffer` trait读取文件描述符到缓冲区，并处理初始化和未初始化部分。同时，文章提到`Buffer` trait的通用性，可用于如`epoll::wait`等返回事件记录的函数。

该方法通过封装不安全操作，提供了一个安全且灵活的API来处理未初始化内存。
44032680.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中未初始化缓冲区的处理及其安全性、性能和复杂性问题

不同观点：
• Pornel认为，未初始化的字节不仅是随机垃圾值，更是安全风险，可能暴露密钥和指针，导致ASLR等安全机制失效。Rust通过强制要求不允许读取未初始化内存来提高安全性，而Rust语言本身已经可以高效使用未初始化缓冲区，但标准库缺少相关API，这引发了关于如何设计最有用和符合人体工学的API的讨论。

• Vgatherps指出，当前Rust的抽象机器设计导致程序员为了满足抽象机器的要求而牺牲性能，且没有实际的好处。他希望有“冻结”内在功能，并提到LLVM和“任何比特模式”特性的相关工作。他感觉Rust中处理未初始化数据过于复杂，像是编译器工程的复杂性泄露到了编程语言中。

• 90s_dev表示，未初始化数据在Rust中的处理对开发者不友好，增加了编程复杂性，尤其是在使用`MaybeUninit`或`mem::uninit()`时。他希望Rust能更好地屏蔽这些复杂性，像C语言一样更直接地处理未初始化内存，尽管C语言中也有未定义行为（UB）。

• Mleonhard认为，完全初始化缓冲区并不会导致效率大幅下降，特别是在IO吞吐量敏感的代码中，通过重用缓冲区可以在启动时只初始化一次。他分享了自己创建的固定缓冲区库。

• Leoh建议，如果为了在Rust程序中提升性能，可以考虑将部分代码用C语言实现，以获得更好的性能表现。

• Briansm质疑Rust作为一个现代安全的C替代品，为什么不直接在所有新缓冲区上进行零初始化，认为Rust在这方面做得不够彻底。

补充讨论：
• Sqrt_1通过C代码示例讨论了未指定值和未定义值的区别，展示了在C语言中读取未初始化内存可能导致的意外行为，强调了未初始化内存处理的复杂性和潜在问题。

争议焦点：
• Rust中处理未初始化缓冲区的设计选择：一方面是安全性与性能的平衡，另一方面是编程复杂性和开发者体验的权衡。开发者对于如何在Rust中更好地处理未初始化内存有不同的期望和需求。

data.title: Instagram Addiction
data.author: gregsadetsky
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己对Instagram上瘾的经历，以及如何尝试戒掉这个不良习惯。他意识到自己每天凌晨四点起床观看短视频长达两三小时，严重影响了生活。尽管短视频有其独特的叙事和喜剧魅力，但其极易上瘾的特性让他感到困扰。作者尝试“冷 turkey”式戒断，卸载应用并离开数月，但重新安装后又陷入反复卸载和安装的循环。他强调，虽然短视频如同“电子毒品”般让人上瘾，但与真正的物质成瘾不同，希望读者能理解其严重性并避免过度沉迷。最终，他意识到控制这种习惯需要强大的自律。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体和科技平台的成瘾性及其应对方法

不同观点：
• **反谷歌和反Meta观点**：[jasonthorsness]认为谷歌和Meta通过让用户无法关闭短视频等成瘾功能，故意让用户浪费时间，这是一种反用户行为。
• **年龄和成瘾体验**：[JKCalhoun]提到自己60岁，成长在没有智能手机的时代，认为无聊其实是创造力的源泉，并分享了自己通过删除电脑游戏来控制时间的经验。他还提到电视时代也有浪费时间的内容。
• **阅读作为替代方案**：[bccdee]和[Brajeshwar]都建议通过阅读来替代手机使用，并提出具体方法如将手机放在远处，专注于书本。
• **个性化算法与内容消费**：[wenc]认为Instagram的算法并不十分智能，自己的内容消费是可控的，且主要在桌面端使用，成瘾性不高。相反，[game_the0ry]则指出Instagram通过视觉内容和社交地位量化（如粉丝数）引发了成瘾。
• **技术解决方案**：[richardgill88]开发了一个Android屏蔽工具来限制手机使用时间，[akovaski]则设置了系统服务来控制夜间使用YouTube的时间。
• **法律和平台设计建议**：[joshdavham]建议通过法律强制社交媒体平台提供关闭算法推荐的选项，类似于LinkedIn的某些设置。

补充讨论：
• **自我管理和习惯调整**：[cjohnson318]通过删除Instagram、使用笔记本记录学习内容来减少手机使用，[MinimalAction]则在寻找有效提醒自己避免无意义内容消费的方法。
• **成功经验分享**：[ahmadtbk]受Cal Newport的《数字极简主义》启发，三年前彻底删除了Instagram，并用节省下来的时间进行阅读和散步，注意力和心理健康显著改善。

争议焦点：
• 社交媒体平台是否故意设计成瘾功能，使用户难以自控。
• 不同年龄层对科技平台成瘾的感受和应对方式的差异。
• 个性化推荐算法是否比传统媒体（如电视）更具成瘾性。

这些讨论展示了不同用户对科技成瘾问题的深刻认识和各自应对策略，同时也反映了社会对科技平台设计伦理的关注。

44046559.article_content:
i was addicted to instagram for about a month. it upended my life enough that i realized that i was living with something new-an undesirable habit. and once i realized this, it seemed like it would be wise to try to address it or at least think about it. easier said than done.
i left instagram for about three to four months cold turkey-i left a video saying i was leaving, then uninstalled the app.
there’s a few things to talk about here. first, as
emily
noted to me, this is why kids today can be so bitter about their relationships with their own phones. kids (which is anyone younger than 43) watch movies from the early 2000s with a kind of wistfulness because, wow, people lived normal, natural lives without phones. maybe it’s obvious to you, but when you’re 43, you completely grew up without phones. phones were an absolutely new thing that happened in the middle of your 43-year old’s life.
i grew up quite familiar with the state of being absolutely bored to the gills. boredom was just a sensation that you had, like pain or hunger. you’d stare in some direction and you’d be bored. but that doesn’t seem to be a thing i feel anymore. now it’s mostly about dealing with self-control and somehow thinking about it all the time. it is not relaxing. the phone is in your pocket. it’s on your body.
i hope i’m not using “addiction” in a way that trivializes it. some people (have to) deal with their own intense relationships with (substances, habits), and i would never want you to think that what i dealt with is the same as that.
obviously, so many forms of addiction have had an enormous impact on so many lives-upending them, transforming them, taking people from one direction (their wishes, dreams, circumstances) to a very opposite one.
i hope it’s clear i am more than sympathetic.
i developed a habit that would break my sleep in a specific way: i would get up at four a.m. and watch reels for about two to three hours.
what’s impressive about that is that two hours for a movie is nothing—it’s one movie. if i had been getting up in the middle of the night every night to watch superman, you’d think, “wow, this guy’s into superman.” i’d probably learn a lot of superman trivia that i could drop into regular conversation. maybe i’d wonder why i didn’t just do that after work as you could easily combine a nine-to-five job with an intense level of superman fandom.
but an instagram reel or any sort of short-form video…—really, “short-form” isn’t strong nor short enough of a word. six seconds isn’t short. it’s instant. it’s zero seconds. there is no difference between zero seconds and six seconds in any timeline unless you build atomic watches or run
time.gov
. if any clock in your house was off by six seconds, you wouldn’t spend any amount of time thinking about that. and yet this new art form can tell a story with multiple edits within a single six-second timeframe.
it’s an incredible achievement. who among us even knows if akira kurosawa could make a good six-second reel? (please don’t use a generative ai to generate 6 second akira kurosawa-styled tiktok videos, even if nothing could ever prevent you from doing this.)
ok but the six-second video format
is
extremely impressive from a narrative, storytelling, and comedy point of view. the art of editing has probably improved globally or developed some sort of new appendix, which i hope doesn’t metastasize into all moviemaking. but cutting your teeth on making a good six-second video must somehow give you incredible editing abilities. i totally get it as a training ground for filmmakers or anyone that’s into storytelling.
that’s the good part. the good part is the fun and addictive part—there are truly incredible videos out there, even though i am not going to link to them. if i told you the story of how heroin felt, i would probably not tell you where to get it. if you truly needed heroin (who needs heroin?), you’d be pursuing it anyway and would probably find your way to some heroin mart. but i hope you don’t do either heroin or short videos. the problem is, short videos are a lot harder to escape.
it was also so obvious to see that not every six-second video was good or seemed interesting to me. in that span of a few hours, i’d get a few—sometimes one, sometimes five, rarely 10—that were the funniest videos i had ever seen in my life. but that’s just a slot machine: you keep pressing the button like a rat and the button gives you drugs, but randomly, which is the worst/best kind of addiction-creating mechanism. it’s why inbox addiction is also a thing (that i have): never knowing when you’ll get an email, you keep reloading until you inevitably get one.
recently, i reinstalled instagram to post a video and a music video, then uninstalled it and reinstalled it and uninstalled it at least six times in the last week. unfortunately, the app felt just as good as before. i’m not sure if the algorithm got better—i understand that this is probably not what happened, and i was just mi

data.author: _morph3ous
data.article_summary: TitleBridge是一款用于Final Cut Pro的工作流工具，方便将字幕作为可编辑标题添加，无需订阅任何服务或离开Final Cut。系统要求包括一台运行Final Cut Pro 11.1及以上版本的Mac，推荐使用Apple Silicon处理器以利用音频转字幕功能。若没有此功能，需手动输入字幕或使用第三方工具。TitleBridge不收集用户信息。如遇问题，可通过页面底部的评论表单反馈，开发者将通过Github私下联系用户解决。

44047530.article_content:
TitleBridge
A Final Cut Pro workflow to make adding captions as titles easy. There is no need to leave Final Cut to add editable titles from your captions and no need to subscribe to any services.
System Requirements
Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or better processor)*
Final Cut Pro 11.1+
* TitleBridge does not require Apple Silicon. We recommend this so Final Cut is able to
transcribe your audio to captions. Without this functionality, you will either need to
manually enter your captions or use a third-party tool. It is much more pleasant and efficient
to be able to do it all from within Final Cut.
Privacy Policy
TitleBridge does not automatically collect or send any information back to us.
Getting Support
If you are having any issues with the application, please let me know in the comment form
at the bottom of this page. Do not include any private information as your comment will
be publicly visible.
The comments are through Github's Giscus, so I will reach out to you privately through your Github
account to figure out the best communication method to continue resolving the issue facing you.
Backstory
The origin story of TitleBridge

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于人类与世界队、引擎在国际象棋比赛中的表现以及与机器的对比。

不同观点：
• sceptic123认为大型语言模型（LLM）通过足够的数据可以找到最佳答案，但训练需要与像Carlsen这样的顶尖棋手对战，而这不太可能实现。
• sfblah暗示世界队在比赛中使用了足够的引擎帮助。
• drewbitt指出世界队达到了95%的准确率，并在下半场发挥了99%的准确率。
• gcbill认为值得考虑的是，这是一场自由式国际象棋而非经典国际象棋，传统开局走法在自由式中不适用。尽管如此，凭借24小时的计算时间，引擎在自由式中可能表现更好。
• gangelov提供了有关比赛的更多细节链接。
• selcuka认为Carlsen有可能获胜，如果世界队没有强迫和棋。在虚拟聊天中，玩家对是否和棋存在分歧。
• hnposter提到这场比赛让他想起了Kasparov对阵The World的比赛。
• tedunangst质疑有多少人的投票是完全一致的。
• nurettin幽默地指出，143000名棋手合并后的水平接近Anish Giri，并认为如果世界队没有作弊，这很有趣。
• EnPissant认为即使世界队拥有最新技术，与引擎相比，他们的概念是有缺陷的，并猜测有人从中获利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于世界队是否在比赛中使用了作弊手段或者过度依赖引擎帮助。

补充讨论：
• 用户对不同语言学习工具的功能、价格和效果进行了比较和讨论，强调了实时对话、多语言支持和互动性在语言学习中的重要性。
• 争议的焦点在于AI生成内容的准确性和用户对不同应用的付费模式的看法。
• 用户普遍关注语言学习应用的功能完善程度和实用性，并愿意分享自己的使用经验和反馈。

通过这些讨论，可以看出用户在选择语言学习工具时，注重个性化体验、多功能性和性价比。同时，开发者们也在不断改进和创新，以满足用户的多样化需求。

data.title: Show HN: I made a word puzzles app for improving your English vocabulary
data.author: tomek_zemla
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为DictionaryGames的网站，专为英语作为第二语言（ESL）的学生、教师和语言爱好者设计。网站提供现代化的单词闪卡和短小的单词游戏，帮助用户扩展词汇量，无需注册和跟踪。免费版已开放试用，而高级版将提供个性化学习应用，适应学习者的语言水平和兴趣，每年25美元，预计2025年春季推出。此外，还有为教师设计的PDF词汇练习，每月10美元，预计2025年秋季推出。文章末尾提供了联系方式以获取产品更新和支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏问题的质量和合理性，以及游戏的收费模式

不同观点：
• [jamesdhutton] 认为游戏有潜力，但目前存在的问题包括问题过难且有些答案不正确。他举例说明，问题给出的答案和实际词义不符，例如将"saddle"作为"负担"的答案是不准确的，因为"saddle"作为名词并没有"负担"的意思。

• [AlexErrant] 提出了一个具体的问题示例，句子的填空答案为"daddy"，他认为这不是一个合理的问题或答案，并建议让母语者审核题库，以提高问题的质量。

• [replwoacause] 也遇到了类似的问题，给出的正确答案"jolly"与自己预期的答案"sufficient"不符，他认为问题设计不合理，令人困惑。

• [we_needit] 对游戏的收费模式提出了质疑，认为既然声称是帮助性的产品，就不应该收费，帮助不应总是以回报为目的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于游戏问题的设计不合理，包括问题难度过大、答案不准确以及题目本身不够恰当。
• 另一个争议点是游戏的收费模式是否合理，部分玩家认为既然是帮助性质的产品，就不应收费。
• 多个评论者都建议对题库进行更严格的审核，以提高问题的准确性和合理性。

data.title: Rethinking Sleep from First Principles
data.author: pedalpete
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了睡眠的传统观念和科学研究，质疑了普遍认为的8小时睡眠规则。作者作为一个长期失眠者，发现仅仅增加睡眠时间并不一定改善睡眠质量。通过从基础原理重新思考睡眠，作者指出睡眠的质量不应仅通过时间衡量，而应关注深度睡眠、纺锤波活动和K-复合波等具体脑活动。深度睡眠对大脑修复、记忆巩固和免疫功能至关重要，但其质量比时间更重要。作者强调，当前的睡眠科学过于关注时间这一易于测量的变量，而忽略了更复杂的脑活动和恢复过程。文章呼吁重新审视睡眠，关注真正影响健康的因素，而非单纯的时间长短。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于通过功能性睡眠健康提升睡眠质量的评论及其可信度

不同观点：
• [florbnit] 认为该提议看似只是为了收集电子邮件地址，通过声称提升睡眠修复功能来吸引注意，但缺乏实质内容。他以讽刺的口吻总结，这像是在说“我读了一些关于睡眠的东西，请把你的电子邮件给我”。

• [tailspin2019] 指出，如果文章能够引用其信息来源，将会更具可信度。目前内容虽然有趣，但很容易被视为仅为搜索引擎优化（SEO）而作，缺乏深度和权威性。

• [al_borland] 批评作者花了大量篇幅抨击8小时睡眠的观念，但并未提供可操作的替代方案。他认为，8小时睡眠是一个大多数人大脑完成必要修复活动的时间基准，而新提议如果没有提供新的、可操作的规则，那么文章的目的就值得怀疑，可能只是为了收集电子邮件地址。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章是否提供了有价值、可操作的睡眠建议，还是仅仅为了获取用户的电子邮件地址。
• 几位评论者都对文章缺乏引用来源表示不满，认为这是影响其可信度的重要因素。
• [al_borland] 特别指出，抨击传统8小时睡眠观念的同时，需要提供新的实用指导，否则提议缺乏实际意义。

44046923.article_content:
Rethinking Sleep from First Principles
If youâre like me, youâve maybe had a love/hate relationship with sleep. As a life-long chronic insomniac, Iâd love to sleep, but itâs never really been a thing for me. I went down the usual path of trying to get 8 hours of sleep, but even when I did, I didnât feel any more refreshed than when I slept for 5 hours. Often, I actually felt better on 5 hours of sleep.
â
One sleepless night, I thought âI didnât care if I slept, I just didnât want to be tired anymoreâ, and that thought led me to do a deep dive into the latest in sleep science, but what I found was disappointing. Mostly, just the same old sleep hygiene recommendations Iâd heard when I was a kid. There has to be more to it! How have people been struggling with sleep for decades and the best we can come up with is âget more sleepâ?
â
It took me a LONG time to break out of the idea that more sleep time meant better sleep. The 8 hour rule has been beaten into us. Itâs a myth that refuses to die.Â
â
So I thought Iâd back up and take a look at sleep from a first principles approach. As much as I can anyway. There is still so much we donât know about sleep, but what we do know, I believe, leads us to a very different path than the one the sleep industry follows, and refuses to give up on.
â
Every animal with a brain has to sleep. Itâs been said that there is no way that evolution would have kept sleep as a requirement if it wasnât absolutely vital to life. For many animals itâs just too dangerous to lose consciousness for an extended period of time. For example, dolphins would drown if they didnât come up for air, so they sleep with only Â½ of their brain at a time. Other animals would become easy prey if they slept, so they only have a very short sleep opportunity. Lions, being the top of the food chain, have little concern for when and how they sleep, and evolution has left them with regular naps throughout the day.
â
But right there we see the problem. Even Iâm referring to sleep by time, when Iâm trying to look from a first principles perspective.
â
â
For a long time, weight was treated as a primary indicator of health. Not because it was the best measure, but because it was easy to collect, and
generally useful at identifying outliers. If someone was severely underweight or morbidly obese, you could safely assume there was a health issue.
â
But for most people, weight alone doesnât say much. It doesnât tell you how someone feels, how well their body is functioning, or how their systems are holding up over time. It doesnât tell you about stress, recovery, immune function, or resilience.
â
Weâve been measuring it by time, not because time is the right variable, but because itâs the one we can see. And like weight, it tells us something at the extremes. But for most people, minutes asleep isnât what determines how well sleep is working.
â
The primary restorative function of sleep is deep sleep, or slow-wave sleep, which again, is often measured by time, but slow-wave sleep isnât time based. A slow-wave is the synchronous firing of neurons which are the foundation of health. This precise brain activity is part of the vital restorative processes that occur during sleep, and slow-waves in particular are tied to the flushing of metabolic waste from the brain, they kick-off a cascade of hormonal responses, they prime the immune system, and it is a time when memories are encoded and stored.Â
â
Deep sleep can be very restorative, if your neurons are firing well, and those processes complete successfully, itâs hugely valuable sleep. However, the same âdeep sleepâ can just as easily have less functional restoration, with lower delta power, when the brain is less capable of repair. Youâve likely felt this after drinking alcohol. You may have had deep sleep, but the restorative function was impaired. As we age, the effectiveness of slow-wave repair declines even if weâre getting an appropriate amount of âtimeâ in deep sleep.
â
Spindle activity is another process tied to memory. These are short bursts of brain activity that seem to help transfer memories into long-term storage. The more spindles you have, the better your memory consolidation tends to be. And unlike deep sleep, we donât measure this by time. You donât track minutes of spindles. You count them like dollar bills, not minutes in a bank account.
â
K-complexes are large electrical bursts that seem to help your brain stay asleep while still monitoring your environment. They often occur when thereâs noise or movement nearby, acting like a gatekeeper. Most of the time, the brain hears something and says, âthatâs not important, keep sleeping.â But sometimes, especially in light sleepers, k-complexes are followed by waking. Itâs the brain deciding it needs to bring you back to awareness.
â

data.article_summary: "Quantum for Everyone" 是一个让量子教育变得简单易懂的倡议，通过视觉化的“量子图像主义”（Quantum Picturalism）来讲解量子概念。这种方法由Bob Coecke和Stefano Gogioso在其书《Quantum in Pictures》中提出，只需使用加减法和角度就能理解复杂的量子理论，无需高深数学知识。量子图像主义通过游戏般的规则，让各个年龄段的学习者都能轻松掌握量子知识，旨在降低学习门槛，使量子教育更具包容性。该项目还提供Discord社区和常见问题解答，帮助初学者更好地入门。

Learn quantum concepts using just addition, subtraction, and angles.
Quantum ideas are often seen as intimidating, which can discourage people from exploring them. We make quantum education accessible by breaking down complex concepts into simple, visual learning experiences.
What is Quantum Picturalism?
Quantum Picturalism is a visual form of math that only requires addition, subtraction, and angles to depict quantum ideas. The approach uses “game-like” rules, and yet it’s rigorous enough for use by quantum experts around the world.
This empowers teachers and learners of all ages by making quantum math accessible and inclusive.
The term, “Quantum Picturalism” was coined to describe this unique approach of teaching quantum concepts visually, reducing intimidation and opening the field to broader audiences.

44023226.article_content:
PG&E Sucks or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Building my own Solar System
Joe Eklund
Follow
24 min read
·
1 day ago
--
5
Listen
Share
W
ell it happened. PG&E has dropped the facade of necessary rate increases because of system upgrades, and they have come out and said what we knew all along:
they only care about profits.
Then they turn around and spit in our faces by telling us our bills are
actually
lower
than they were a year ago
. And if you really want to get your blood boiling, go
read this nonsense from their CEO
.
Last year I got sick of it and started looking at deploying a solar system, and that was before
PG&E decided to have 6 rate hikes (#7 on the way)
. Now a year later, my solar system is up and running, and I no longer cringe anytime I hear the AC kick on in the Bay Area heat (we can’t all live in SF). Here’s how I did it.
Fair warning, I am going to go deep into the weeds on some things. Feel free to skip over sections you find boring or you can even skip to the end if you want to read my lessons learned.
But first, a haiku to summarize the current state of power providers in California:
PG&E sucks
I hate the CPUC
This is all a scam
I received no compensation from any of the companies listed in this article. All thoughts and opinions are my own.
Table of Contents
But Why?
Research
The Build
Lessons Learned
But Why?
I definitely don’t have a problem
Aside from the obvious that PG&E rates are entering ludacris mode, I am a self-hoster. I have a rack in the garage that pulls a little less than 1kw. That’s 1kw 24/7/365. And though I have a garage fan that keeps it cool eight months of the year (and at night), in the summer I have a portable A/C that pulls about 800w when it’s running. It gets hot here, way hotter than what most folks think of when they hear Bay Area. Last summer there were months of an electrical bill north of $1200. Yikes.
You may now be thinking, well why do I need a rack that pulls 1kw? I guess I don’t, but the word
downsize
is not in my vocabulary. Maybe I’ll go over my self-hosting setup in some future articles if there is interest.
Research
Information Overload
As I began researching, it became apparent there were two paths I could take: a small system to offset my constant rack usage or a large system to reduce my need for PG&E (electricity at least — gas is another story) as much as possible.
The rabbit hole then started going deeper: Do it myself? Have a company do it? Batteries? Enphase? Microinverters? Monofacial/Bifacial panels? What is NEM 2/3? How do I rack the panels? Inside or outside the garage for batteries? City planning and inspection? The list goes on and on and can be overwhelming.
Eventually I decided that I wanted a full system to try and completely kill my electricity bill, not just a small system to offset the rack usage.
I figured the next step was to get some quotes for systems from local solar companies. Even if I ended up doing it myself, I could see ballpark pricing and see what kind of system they recommended. I found three companies and gave them my PG&E usage for the past year (about 16,000 kwh) and got three quotes ranging from ~45 — 55k.
But the catch was those systems all drastically undersized the battery in my opinion: they ranged from 5 — 15kwh. In the summer (when electricity is even more expensive), my rack + portable A/C + house A/C (3 ton) could easily be pulling 6kw. That’s not even accounting for other appliances like the microwave or stove.
I could easily burn through the batteries in just a few hours. This
would
at least stop me from pulling power during peak cost TOU hours (4–9PM), but the rest of the night I’d be pulling from PG&E. Also, once you go solar/batteries you actually have a wider time period of peak pricing, called partial peak, that goes all the way to midnight —
E-ELEC
. Now is a good time to talk about
Net Energy Metering (NEM)
.
Net Energy Metering (NEM)
NEM is the agreement you have with PG&E that takes into account the energy you generate and the energy you use. Before 2017, customers would be on NEM 1, which offered the best incentives: free connection and the best export rates. Between 2017 and 2023 customers who installed new solar systems were put on NEM 2. There were a few additional costs passed onto consumers like slightly increased connection fees, but the actual rate you received from PG&E for your generation was the same. Then NEM 3 came in 2023 and the main changes were further increased connection fees and reduced export rates (by about 75%). Eventually everyone will be bumped to NEM 3, but many folks are grandfathered in on NEM 2 for 10–20 years.
NEM 3 means when you generate electricity, PG&E will pay you pennies on the dollar, then turn around and sell it back to you at inflated costs when you are no longer producing solar (i.e. at night).
The solution to this is to install a battery system, but batteries are
expensive
. Really expensive. Though I didn’t proceed with additional quotes for

data.title: Convolutions, Polynomials and Flipped Kernels
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讲解了多项式乘法与卷积和之间的关系。首先，文章通过一个具体例子展示了如何进行多项式乘法，例如将$(3x^3 + x^2 + 2x + 1)$与$(2x^2 + 6)$相乘，通过交叉相乘并合并同类项得到结果。

接着，文章提出了一种不同的方法，通过表格展示每个输出项的系数是如何由输入多项式的系数相乘并相加得到的。文章进一步引入了一种抽象表示法，将多项式表示为系数的和，并通过公式$S_k = \sum_{i} P_i \cdot R_{k-i}$计算乘积多项式的系数。

文章还介绍了一种图形方法，通过翻转一个多项式并逐项相乘来得到结果，这实际上与计算两个数组的卷积相同。最后，文章简要提及了信号与系统的理论，指出多项式乘法与卷积在离散信号处理中的等价性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：概率分布、卷积、生成函数以及多项式乘法在数学中的应用

不同观点：
• [incognito124] 认为可以通过卷积来证明，如果有两个不同的概率分布 X 和 Y，那么 X+Y 的概率分布是 X 和 Y 的概率质量函数（PMF）或概率密度函数（PDF）的卷积。这强调了卷积在概率论中的应用。

This is a post about multiplying polynomials, convolution sums and the
connection between them.
Multiplying polynomials
Suppose we want to multiply one polynomial by another:
\[(3x^3+x^2+2x+1)\cdot(2x^2+6)\]
This is basic middle-school math - we start by cross-multiplying:
\[6x^5+2x^4+4x^3+2x^2+18x^3+6x^2+12x+6\]
And then collect all the terms together by adding up the coefficients:
\[6x^5+2x^4+22x^3+8x^2+12x+6\]
Let's look at a slightly different way to achieve the same result. Instead of
cross multiplying all terms and then adding up, we'll focus on what terms appear
in the output, and for each such term - what its coefficients are going to be.
This is easy to demonstrate with a table, where we lay out one polynomial
horizontally and the other vertically. Note that we have to be explicit about
the zero coefficient of
x
in the second polynomial:
The diagonals that add up to each term in the output are highlighted. For example,
to get the coefficient of
x^3
in the output, we have to add up:
The coefficient of
x^3
in the first polynomial, multiplied by the
constant (coefficient of
x^0
) in the second polynomial
The coefficient of
x^2
in the first polynomial, multiplied by the
coefficient of
in the second polynomial
The coefficient of
in the first polynomial, multiplied by the
coefficients of
x^2
in the second polynomial
(if the second polynomial had a
x^3
term, there would be another
component to add)
For what follows, let's move to a somewhat more abstract representation: a
polynomial
P
can be represented as a sum of coefficients
P_i
multiplied by corresponding powers of
x
[1]
:
\[P=\sum_{i}P_i x^i\]
Suppose we have two polynomials,
P
and
R
. When we multiply them together,
the resulting polynomial is
S
. Based on our insight from the table diagonals
above, we can say that for each
k
:
\[S_k=\sum_{i}P_i\cdot R_{k-i}\]
And then the entire polynomial
S
is:
\[S=\sum_{k} \left( \sum_{i}P_i\cdot R_{k-i}\right)x^k\]
It's important to understand this formulation, since it's key to this
post. Let's use our example polynomials to see how it works. First, we represent
the two
polynomials as sequences of coefficients (starting with 0, so the coefficient
of the constant is first, and the coefficient of the highest power is last):
\[P=[1,2,1,3]\qquad R=[6,0,2]\]
In this notation,
P_0
is the first element in the list for
P
, etc.
To calculate the coefficient of
x^3
in the product:
\[S_3=\sum_{i}P_i\cdot R_{3-i}\]
Expanding the sum for all the non-zero coefficients of
P
:
\[S_3=P_0 R_3+P_1 R_2+P_2 R_1+P_3 R_0=0+4+0+18=22\]
Similarly, we'll find that
S_4=2
,
S_2=8
and so on, resulting
in the final polynomial as before:
\[6x^5+2x^4+22x^3+8x^2+12x+6\]
There's a nice graphical approach to multiply polynomials using this idea of
pairing up sums for each term in the output:
We start with the diagram on the left: one of the polynomials remains in its
original form, while the other is flipped around (constant term first, highest
power term last). We line up the polynomials vertically, and multiply the
corresponding coefficients: the constant coefficient of the output is just the
constant coefficient of the first polynomial times the constant coefficient of
the second polynomial.
The diagram on the right shows the next step: the second polynomial is shifted
left by one term and lined up vertically again. The corresponding coefficients
are multiplied, and then the results are added to obtain the coefficient of
x
in the output polynomial.
We continue the process by shifting the lower polynomial left:
Calculating the coefficients of
x^2
and then
x^3
. A couple more
steps:
Now we have all the coefficients of the output. Take a moment to convince
yourself that this approach is equivalent to the summation shown just
before it, and also to the "diagonals in a table" approach shown further up.
They all calculate the same thing
[2]
!
Hopefully it should be clear why the second polynomial is "flipped" to perform
this procedure. This all comes down to which input terms pair up to calculate
each output term. As seen above:
\[S_k=\sum_{i}P_i\cdot R_{k-i}\]
While the index
i
moves in one direction (from the low power terms to the
high power terms) in
P
, the index
k-i
moves in the opposite direction in
R
.
If this procedure reminds you of computing a convolution between two arrays,
that's because it's exactly that!

data.title: Clojuring the web application stack: Meditation One
data.author: adityaathalye
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了使用Clojure进行web开发的栈结构和哲学思考。作者解释了Clojure web应用的基本架构，包括业务逻辑、Ring库、应用服务器（如Jetty）等组件的交互。文章还讨论了框架的作用和局限，认为框架是一种工业自动化形式，虽然简化了选择和流程，但也可能限制开发者的思维。作者对比了新手、中级、专家和大师级开发者对框架的不同依赖程度，并强调Clojure世界倾向于不依赖传统框架，而是通过函数和库实现功能。文章最后提到，构建web应用是进入软件行业的重要途径，而Clojure提供了一种不同于框架的开发方式。文章还提供了作者的相关演讲链接和一个示例项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Clojure生态中的 web 开发框架与依赖管理

不同观点：
• **adityaathalye** 认为，Clojure社区中构建web应用的默认方式是从生产级库中自行组合堆栈，而不是使用一体化框架。这种方法有利有弊，类似于传统web框架的情况。他强调从基本原则开始构建应用，并分享了他对这种方法的理解和经验。

• **elchief** 提供了Metabase作为一个使用Clojure编写的大型web应用的例子，指出其源代码可以作为参考，以了解如何在大型项目中管理依赖和架构。

• **wink** 指出，自行组合堆栈的方式在小项目或业余项目中可能导致依赖管理复杂化，尤其是在升级时。他提到在Rails或某些PHP框架中，依赖较少且升级过程简单，而在Clojure项目中，可能会有更多的依赖和移动部件，增加了管理负担。他认为一个可靠的项目发布流程可以减轻这种负担。

• **librasteve** 对adityaathalye的帖子表示欣赏，并计划将其经验应用于自己的项目(Harcstack)。他提到自己相信HTMX在UX动态性方面的作用，但不确定它如何与其他部分结合。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Clojure开发中自行组合堆栈的方式在灵活性和控制力上的优势，与依赖管理和升级的复杂性之间的权衡。wink强调了在小项目中管理多个依赖的实际困难，而adityaathalye和librasteve则更关注于从基本原则构建应用的潜在好处和个人偏好。

• **例子和论据**：
  - Metabase项目被用作Clojure在大型web应用中的实际例子。
  - wink以Rails和PHP框架为例，说明依赖管理在小项目中的不同体验。
  - HTMX和其他技术在librasteve的项目中的潜在应用被提及，以讨论UX动态性。

以上观点展示了Clojure开发中不同开发者对框架选择和依赖管理的不同看法，以及各自在实际项目中的经验和偏好。

Update (2024-09-04):
I just published a complete project that follows up the concepts set up in this post.
adityaathalye/usermanager-first-principles
is a stripped-down variant of
seancorfield/usermanager-example
. The project README explains all.
Errors and inaccuracies are all mine
1
. If you spot any, please write to
complaints
@ my domain. (And if you want to say nice things, write to
compliments
@ my domain :). Feel free to discuss on HackerNews (
here
) and r/Clojure (
here
).
A basic grounding in the Clojure programming language is assumed
2
. Familiarity with web development will help.
I will stick to discussing the Clojure web application stack in relation to classical Web Frameworks. Primarily
3
.
Yes, a
Meditation Two
is in draft hell. It is about
Getting Pretty Deep In The Woods
. If it sees the light of day, it will also be a giant post. Lambda help us.
Getting Parable-ic
Multitudes of sworn "Rails developer"s, "Laravel developer"s, "Django developer"s, "Next.js developer"s and suchlike throng the universe…
Why?
Novices don't know they don't know.
The Framework
saves them from themselves.
So they survive.
Intermediates know enough but would rather not
have
to.
But
it is a living. A person must eat.
So that's that. RTFM.
Experts know enough to care deeply
4
.
The Framework
is muscle memory; all the hacks,
the tricks, the deep dark secrets.
It bends to will. Mostly.
Masters know enough to not roll their own.
And yet… sometimes they do.
A new cycle begins.
Once upon a time, there was one.
WebObjects
.
Now they are numberless.
Getting the Big Picture
Picture the Clojure web stack this way… to a good first approximation:
Our business logic (written in Clojure),
relies on a bunch of Clojure libraries (frequently, ring-clojure),
that know how to use an application server (Jetty).
In the simplest deployment model, this picture fits within a single compute instance (e.g. a PC, Cloud VM, or "Serverless" container).

But before getting too practical, an indulgent philosophical interlude.
Getting Philosophical
I think frameworks are a form of industrial automation (of choices, behaviour, workflows, detail and so forth). Perceived this way, they embody the tradeoffs of industrial automation
5
.
Tim Ewald makes astute observations about this phenomenon, in his talk "
Clojure: Programming with Hand Tools
". As he remarks, pervasive use of automation has the insidious quality of changing how we view the world and how we perceive problems. To a mind invested in
a
framework, all web software will look irresistibly framework shaped. Squint just right, and the answer reveals itself. And they may very well be right. Until they are not.
The Clojure world does it the hard way; viz. the not-framework way.

• [zeta0134] 分享了将游戏翻译成Toki Pona的经验，认为尽管有趣，但由于词汇量小，难以找到明确表达游戏机制的方法，同时指出社区对使用阿拉伯数字作为替代方案的接受度较高。

补充讨论：
• [EdwardDiego] 提到了语言与思维关系的理论（Sapir-Worf假设），暗示Toki Pona这种极简语言可能是该理论的极端应用，反映了一种对语言影响思维的特别关注。
• 争议的焦点集中在Toki Pona的语言简化及其在实际应用中的局限性，如词汇不足和语法错误等问题。

data.title: Taito-tastic: Kiki Kaikai and its Hardware
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文主要讨论了Taito的游戏《Kiki KaiKai》及其硬件架构。作者首先纠正了一个误解，即Neo Geo并不是唯一大量使用精灵图的硬件，其他公司如ADK和NEC早在1970年代就采用了类似技术。接着，文章介绍了《Kiki KaiKai》这款1986年的射击游戏，强调其操作难度和独特的美学风格，但也指出其控制方式不够灵活，不像《Smash TV》或《Ikari Warriors》那样使用双摇杆。

硬件方面，文章详细描述了《Kiki KaiKai》的黑色PCB板及其主要组件，包括YM2203 FM合成器和Z80 CPU。还提到了Taito定制的JPH1020P微控制器和用于存储调色板信息的PROM芯片。文章特别指出，Taito的系统放弃了传统的图块层，完全依赖精灵图层，并猜测了TMM2064P-70 RAM芯片的实际速度。

总体而言，本文通过分析《Kiki KaiKai》的游戏玩法和硬件结构，揭示了1980年代街机游戏技术的某些特点和发展。

44021841.article_content:
So some concepts got stuck in my head early on when looking into hardware that just donât hold. One of these was that the Neo Geo was unique because of its heavy use of sprites where other systems would use tilemaps. But thatâs not unique to the Neo Geo: ADK was just upgrading their
Alpha68k
family, which all used the same system. Epoch and NECâs
ÂµPD777
did the same thing in the 1970âs for home gamers. And now Taito. Sprite-centric hardware wasnât unique to SNK at all.
Kiki KaiKai
Sometimes a company grabs another companyâs series and runs with it. Thatâs what happened with
Kiki KaiKai
, Taitoâs Shinto-themed shoot âem upâ you probably know it better for Natsumeâs take on the concept, released under the name
Pocky & Rocky
.
Pocky & Rocky with Becky
is an amazing game title and you will not convince me otherwise.
And honestly, 1986âs
Kiki KaiKai
is a lot rougher than
Pocky & Rocky
. Itâs an unforgiving shoot âem up, where the player is on ground level, so has to also interact with terrain on the map. Specifically, as a shrine maiden, you can attack with
ofuda
paper cards and use a
gohei
wand as a short-range attack.
Kiki KaiKai
is also really hard and unforgiving. But it shares its flaws with a lot of games of its style from the time. See, the problem is your attacks are limited to go in the same eight directions you can move, and the direction you shoot is the same as the direction you move.
Some games like
Smash TV
resolved this with twin joysticks for shooting. SNKâs
Ikari Warriors
(not the Micronics NES port, the arcade one) used a single joystick that could be rotated in addition to its usual directional behavior.
Kiki Kaikai
would have been better if it was a twin-stick shooter, but it is not.
So Iâm not going to give you a review of
Kiki Kaikai
, other than to say I
love
the gameâs aesthetic. Plus, when you get a game over (I got a lot of them) you get this pinball-style ânumber matchâ game, which makes me wonder why you didnât see this more often in arcades. You can disable this with a DIP switch if youâre a philistine.
Anyways, I suspect most of my readers came here for the hardware anyway.
The hardware!
Kiki KaiKai
runs on a black PCB. Donât mind the taped up port at the end; apparently similar hardware used for Taitoâs
Kick and Run
can hook up two PCBs for a four player game, but for this game thereâs no such luck. Letâs start diggig in with the music section.
The centerpiece of this is the YM2203 FM synthesizer. On this blog alone you might remember this from
the Alpha68k
board
, Data Eastâs
Gate of Doom
,
The Legend of Makai
, and even the â3-voiceâ FM sound board on my
NEC PC-9821 V13
. Definitely a popular choice, and pairing it with a Z80 CPU is no surprise either.
The JPH1020P with its very cute label is a Taito-branded MCU based off of the Motorola 6801 family of 8-bit microcontrollers. Microcontrollers with built-in ROM (in this case, just 4kiB) were popular with some arcade manufacturers as theyâre harder to dump and therefore clone, but donât worry, this oneâs dumped
and in MAME
. Despite being closer to the sound CPU on the board, it has access to a small amount of RAM shared with the main CPU.
The CPU area is also not a surprise. Weâve got another Z80, and you can also see some PROMs; those stamped A85-08, A85-09, and A85-10 are the palette PROMs, a common technique used in those days. This is 12-bit RGB color, which is nothing to sneeze at in 1986. Or today. Donât sneeze on the PCB, thatâs gross. A85-07, as well as some other chips scattered across the board marked similarly to the PROMs, are actually PALs; programmable array logic. This helps make the board more compact than something like the
Sega System 1
, which was contemporary though getting on in years at this time.
The heart of any 1980s arcade board is its visual circuitry. The Sega System 1 worked in a very common way at the time: tilemap layers and sprite layers, with separate ROMs for each; the tilemap is a grid of tiles that can be scrolled as a unit, and the sprites are moveable line-buffered objects. Sometimes the ROMs were not physically separate, as in the obscure
Nintendo Entertainment System
. Taitoâs system here, though, forgoes the tilemap entirely.
One thing I find interesting are the TMM2064P-70 RAM chips in the lower corner of the image. Looking at the datasheet for the TMM2064 series of RAM chips, thereâs no 70 access class listed.
Now, following the naming scheme literally, youâd expect that a TMM2064P-70 would have a 700ns RAM chip. That would be exceedingly slow, thoughâ my guess, combined with the fact that â70â is clearly stamped on after the fact, is that these are TMM2064P chips that have been tested and certified to work at even faster speeds like 70ns. Generally the fastest RAM you need on a board like this is for the linebuffer, so thatâd be my guess here.
Thereâs one interesting consequence of Taitoâs sprite-based

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对基于web的编辑器Kraa的评价和反馈，包括其功能、用途、用户体验及技术问题。

不同观点：
• **质疑实用性与需求**：[mrweasel]和[frank20022]对该编辑器的实际用途提出质疑，尤其是与本地文件管理相比，他们不理解为何需要一个基于web的编辑器。同时，他们关注文件存储位置、导出功能（如Wordpress、Git）以及与其他工具（如Notion）相比的独特优势。[mrweasel]特别提到对文件存储在浏览器中的不适。
  
• **技术问题与用户体验**：[zeroq]提出了使用中的技术问题，特别是返回按钮的异常行为，指出应用在浏览器历史记录管理上存在bug。这与其他用户如[alexnewman]提到网站似乎宕机的问题类似，表明部分用户遇到了稳定性或技术故障。

• **积极反馈与支持**：一些用户如[abdullahajmal]、[yasir326]和[patrick4urcloud]对Kraa的界面设计表示赞赏，称其干净、简洁、无干扰。此外，[bertocast]表示自己一直在寻找类似的工具，并对Kraa表示感谢。[thestepafter]和[chrisvalleybay]则对编辑器的聊天功能和多人对话体验给予了正面评价，甚至联想到Google Wave。

• **功能需求与竞争比较**：[GuillaumeAirGen]提出了一个具体问题，即为什么要从Notion切换到Kraa，要求明确的功能优势和理由。

补充讨论：
• **展示与协作功能**：[levmiseri]分享了一个公共展示链接，展示了Kraa的聊天功能，特别是其独特的“writer”角色，似乎试图展示Kraa在协作方面的潜力。
  
• **用户年龄与技术代沟**：[mrweasel]提到自己可能因为年龄原因更倾向于传统的文件管理方式，暗示可能存在技术代沟，即年轻用户更容易接受基于浏览器的文件管理方式。

争议焦点：  
• **Kraa的定位与用途**：部分用户质疑Kraa的实际用途和价值主张，尤其是在已经有很多其他无干扰编辑器的情况下。同时，文件存储和导出的问题也是争议的焦点之一。

data.title: Disabling kernel functions in your process (2009)
data.author: rolph
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了使用 `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter` 捕获未处理异常时遇到的问题。Direct3D 和 Flash 等库会频繁安装自己的异常处理器，覆盖主程序的设置，导致崩溃报告无法生成。为解决此问题，作者通过代码修改禁用了 `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`，防止其被其他库覆盖。具体方法是使用 `GetProcAddress` 获取函数地址，并修改其前五字节汇编代码，使其直接返回零，从而使其失效。该方法通过调试验证后，成功实现了稳定捕获未处理异常的功能。尽管涉及代码修改，但作者认为只要谨慎操作，风险可控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows应用程序崩溃时的小型转储（minidump）处理方案及相关的系统保护机制

不同观点：
• Const-me：认为不需要复杂的技巧来处理应用程序崩溃时的小型转储。他们指出Windows错误报告（Windows Error Reporting, WER）组件已经足够灵活，可以通过在注册表中写入一些值来实现该功能，而无需使用其他“hack”方法。如果需要更好的用户体验或在应用程序崩溃时立即压缩和上传小型转储（而不是在下次启动时处理），Const-me建议通过创建一个监督程序（supervisor app）来解决，该程序可以启动主程序并监控其退出，然后处理生成的dmp文件。

• c-linkage：分享了一个相关的经验，提到一个库更改了FPU（浮点单元）设置，导致问题。虽然最终通过在库初始化后重置FPU设置解决了问题，但找出这个问题花费了很长时间。这一评论暗示了外部库可能对系统设置产生意外影响，强调了在调试过程中识别这些影响的难度。

• unilynx：对解决方案表示赞赏，但提出疑问，认为Windows应该有足够的内存保护机制，防止应用程序重写自己的内存，尤其是在函数已经存在于DLL中的情况下，而不是即时编译（JIT-generated）的代码。这表明了对系统安全性和保护机制的关注。

补充讨论：
• Const-me提到了具体的技术实现细节，包括使用CreateProcess启动应用程序以及通过WER自动生成dmp文件，并建议在应用程序退出后处理这些文件，以实现更及时的崩溃处理。
• c-linkage的评论提醒开发者注意外部库可能引发的意外问题，尤其是在调试复杂系统时。
• unilynx的评论引发了对Windows内存保护机制的讨论，质疑是否需要额外的保护措施来防止应用程序修改自身代码，特别是在使用DLL的情况下。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否需要依赖Windows内置的错误报告机制还是采用额外的应用程序层级的处理方案。Const-me认为内置机制足够，而其他评论则关注潜在的外部库问题和系统保护机制的有效性。

44047741.article_content:
Detecting and reporting unhandled exceptions with SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
seemed logical, and, in fact, it worked...  for a while.  Eventually, we started to notice failures that
should
have been reported as a last-chance exception but weren't.  After much investigation, we discovered that
both
Direct3D
and
Flash were installing their own unhandled exception filters!  Worse, they were fighting over it, installing their handlers several times per second!  In practice, this meant our last-chance crash reports were rarely generated, convincing us our crash metrics were better than they were.  (Bad, bad libraries!)
It's pretty ridiculous that we had to solve this problem, but, as Avery Lee says,
"Just because it is not your fault does not mean it is not your problem."
The obvious solution is to join the fray, calling
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
every frame, right?  How about we try something a bit more reliable...  I hate implementing solutions that have obvious flaws.  Thus, we chose to disable (with code modification) the
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
function immediately after installing our own handler.  When Direct3D and Flash try to call it, their requests will be ignored, leaving our exception handler installed.
Code modification...  isn't that scary?  With
a bit
of
knowledge
and defensive programming, it's not that bad.  In fact, I'll show you the code up front:
// If this doesn't make sense, skip the code and come back!
void lockUnhandledExceptionFilter() {
HMODULE kernel32 = LoadLibraryA("kernel32.dll");
Assert(kernel32);
if (FARPROC gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter = GetProcAddress(kernel32, "SetUnhandledExceptionFilter")) {
unsigned char expected_code[] = {
0x8B, 0xFF, // mov edi,edi
0x55,       // push ebp
0x8B, 0xEC, // mov ebp,esp
};
// only replace code we expect
if (memcmp(expected_code, gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(expected_code)) == 0) {
unsigned char new_code[] = {
0x33, 0xC0,       // xor eax,eax
0xC2, 0x04, 0x00, // ret 4
};
BOOST_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(expected_code) == sizeof(new_code));
DWORD old_protect;
if (VirtualProtect(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code), PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &old_protect)) {
CopyMemory(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, new_code, sizeof(new_code));
DWORD dummy;
VirtualProtect(gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code), old_protect, &dummy);
FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), gpaSetUnhandledExceptionFilter, sizeof(new_code));
}
}
}
FreeLibrary(kernel32);
}
If that's obvious to you, then great: We're
hiring
!
Otherwise, here is an overview:
Use
GetProcAddress
to grab the real address of
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
.  (If you just type
&SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
you'll get the relocatable import thunk, not the actual
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
function.)
Most Windows functions begin with five bytes of prologue:
mov edi, edi ; 2 bytes for
hotpatching
support
push ebp     ; stack frame
mov ebp, esp ; stack frame (con't)
We want to replace those five bytes with
return 0;
.  Remember that
__stdcall
functions return values in the
eax
register.  We want to replace the above code with:
xor eax, eax ; eax = 0
ret 4        ; pops 4 bytes (arg) and returns
Also five bytes!  How convenient!  Before we replace the prologue, we verify that the first five bytes match our expectations.  (If not, we can't feel comfortable about the effects of the code replacement.)  The
VirtualProtect
and
FlushInstructionCache
calls are standard fare for code modification.
After implementing this, it's worth stepping through the assembly in a debugger to verify that
SetUnhandledExceptionFilter
no longer has any effect.  (If you really enjoy writing unit tests, it's definitely possible to unit test the desired behavior.  I'll leave that as an exercise for the reader.)
Finally, our last-chance exception reporting actually works!

不同观点：

• Const-me提到了具体的技术实现细节，包括使用CreateProcess启动应用程序以及通过WER自动生成dmp文件，并建议在应用程序退出后处理这些文件，以实现更及时的崩溃处理。

data.title: Oskar Kokoschka, Hermine Moos, and the Alma Mahler Doll
data.author: Goodbichon
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了奥地利艺术家奥斯卡·柯克西卡（Oskar Kokoschka）对作曲家阿尔玛·马勒（Alma Mahler）的痴迷情感。1912年，柯克西卡受托为阿尔玛绘制肖像，尽管初次见面并不顺利，他仍通过大量情书打动了她。两人关系充满激情与痛苦，柯克西卡的嫉妒和占有欲极强，甚至不允许阿尔玛家中出现其已故丈夫古斯塔夫的痕迹。阿尔玛怀孕后堕胎，两人关系恶化。1918年，柯克西卡仍无法忘怀阿尔玛，他联系慕尼黑的玩偶制作者赫尔米娜·穆斯（Hermine Moos），委托她制作一个真人大小、以阿尔玛为原型的玩偶，细节要求极为具体。尽管穆斯接受了项目，但最终玩偶并未让柯克西卡满意。

Oskar Kokoschka, Hermine Moos, and the Alma Mahler Doll
The Alma Mahler doll in artist Hermine Moos’ apartment, juxtaposed with a sketch, likely by Oskar Kokoschka, ca. 1919 —
Source
.
When Oskar Kokoschka fell in love with Alma Mahler, he fell harder than Satan into Hell. “What you are, I am: if you turn from me, I am once again like no one and have no world”, he
wrote
on April 26, 1912. “I live in you, and I only live truly and really for as long as you believe in me.” They had met, by some accounts, while the thirty-two-year-old composer was still wearing a mourning veil; her husband, Gustav Mahler, had died the previous spring. Oskar had been asked to paint Alma’s portrait by her stepfather, but the Viennese artist didn’t make the best of
first impressions
. He was twenty-six, appeared impoverished, and kept coughing up blood. “He hardly spoke, and yet seemed unable to draw. We stood up—and suddenly he embraced me passionately. But this kind of embrace was strange and alien. I did not respond at all—and exactly that seemed to affect him. He stormed out.”
But he won her over with words,
delivering
“the most beautiful love letter” a few days later. Some four hundred more would follow. “The three years with him were a hefty love-battle. Never before have I tasted so many spasms, so much hell and so much paradise”, Alma would
recall
. Oskar’s jealousy was immeasurable. Early in their relationship, he would pass the night pacing before her window while whistling, supposedly guarding against clandestine lovers but actually keeping her awake till dawn. Even the dead did not escape his envy. “Because I am superstitious”, he would
admit
in his autobiography, “I had always insisted that nothing of the dead Gustav Mahler, not even his bust of Rodin, should be brought into our house.” His art became a place to express his fears and passion: he drew her having sex with other men; he drew her spinning yarn with his own intestines. Family and friends witnessed the
amour fou
’s effect upon the couple. “If you see Oskar again, I’ll shoot you”, his mother, Romana — who referred to Alma as “Circe” — once
threatened
.

Visiting her sister in Baden Baden in September, 1912, Alma confirmed what she had suspected since late July: she was pregnant. She quickly returned to Vienna, to an empty flat, only to be
confronted
by the face of her dead husband, whose death mask had been installed in their living room without her consent — the latest paroxysm of Oskar’s obsession. “I suddenly felt: I am not Oskar’s wife!” She had an abortion in mid-October; he
insisted
on pocketing a bloodied cotton pad from the operation: “This is my only child and always will be.” Several years of agony followed, peppered with inconsistent pleasures. Alma eventually resumed an intimate correspondence with Bauhaus founder Walter Gropius; Oskar enlisted in the Austrian cavalry in 1914 at the outbreak of World War I.
In 1918, after years of war — and after recovering from a bayonet wound in Vienna and shellshock in Dresden — Oskar was still thinking of Alma. She had married Gropius in 1915, but the veteran’s need to possess her did not abate. And so he did what few would (hopefully) ever think to do: he
wrote
to the puppet maker Hermine Moos in Munich, who was rumored to have once served as Alma’s seamstress, and inquired about the possibility of recreating his lover as a life-size doll. “Should you be successful, dear Miss Moos, in projecting such a feat of legerdemain that the woman of my dreams will seem to come alive to my eyes and touch, I shall be deeply indebted to your inventiveness and feminine sensibility.”

Moos was his second choice: the well-regarded designer Lotte Pritzel had declined the project after seeing Oskar’s sketches. His instructions were obsessively
detailed

He
fixated
on the doll’s intimate bits, which were meant to be made from “fine, curly horsehair”, reclaimed from a disinfected sofa, and “pouches stuffed with down, cottonwool for the seat and breasts”. Oskar was at least part

data.title: Understanding How Violet Light Can Stop Myopia Progression
data.author: plun9
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了紫光如何通过一种名为OPN5的光感受器蛋白来阻止近视的进展。近视是由于眼球 elongation 导致的视力问题，全球尤其亚洲地区发病率较高。此前研究发现紫光能阻止近视进展，而最新的研究揭示了其作用机制。OPN5蛋白对紫光敏感，能够在紫光下防止眼球过度 elongation 和脉络膜变薄。缺乏OPN5的实验鼠在紫光下未能阻止近视进展。研究表明，紫光通过调节眼内多巴胺水平来发挥作用，这对预防高度近视及其引发的视力问题具有重要意义。预计到2050年，全球近视人口将达50亿，这一发现对公共健康有重大影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于近视（myopia）成因及其潜在疗法的研究讨论

不同观点：
• CommenterPerson认为，过去的研究显示移居到澳大利亚的亚洲儿童近视发生率较低，可能与更多时间在户外活动有关。他们引用了相关文章支持这一观点，强调环境因素对近视的影响。
• Terr_则关注光疗（特别是紫光疗法）对近视的潜在影响，指出紫光（380nm）与常见的LED红蓝光不同，可能有不同的效果。此外，Terr_还提到了蓝光在夜间对生物节律的影响，并表达了对自制强光源可能损害视网膜的担忧。

补充讨论：
• CommenterPerson引用的研究侧重于环境因素（如户外活动时间）对近视的影响，而Terr_的评论更关注光谱中特定波长的光对眼睛的潜在治疗效果及风险。
• Terr_进一步提出了实际操作中可能遇到的问题，例如如何避免紫外线对眼睛的伤害，以及蓝光在夜间对人体生物钟的干扰。
• 争议的焦点可能在于光疗法的有效性和安全性，尤其是在不同波长的光对眼睛的潜在影响方面。Terr_对具体波长的关注和对自制光源的担忧，显示了对该疗法实际应用中的谨慎态度。

总结来看，讨论围绕近视成因的环境因素和光疗法的潜在效果及风险展开，参与者提供了不同的视角和关注点。

Understanding How Violet Light Can Stop Myopia Progression
Posted May 25, 2021
The expression pattern of the photoreceptor protein OPN5 in a mouse retina. The protein is sensitive to violet light and, as reported in a new study from a group of international researchers, plays an important role in the ability of violet light to stop the progression of myopia. This violet light effect has been previously reported, but now researchers are beginning to understand how it works. The prevalence of myopia has been growing worldwide, and it is especially common in Asian countries.
An international team of researchers has taken an important step toward understanding a powerful potential treatment for myopia, which is fast becoming a public health crisis in Asia.
Previous work found that violet light can stop the progression of myopia, an elongation of the eye between the cornea and the retina that results in nearsightedness where far-away objects appear blurry. Now researchers at Keio University in Japan, Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, the Georgia Institute of Technology, and Emory University have discovered that the protective effects of violet light depend on a newly discovered photoreceptor protein in the eye called OPN5, or neuropsin, which was known to be sensitive to violet light.
“Among all the light that reaches our eyes, we have known for sure that violet light is special,” says
Toshihide Kurihara, M.D., Ph.D., assistant professor at Keio University in Japan
. “The human eye seems to use it as a clue to control its size, whereas we knew neither the mechanism nor the necessity behind this phenomenon. We believe to elucidate this mystery might be the key to stop myopia pandemic and worked on it for years.”
A few years ago, the Keio team reported that violet light could prevent myopia progression. Violet light is abundant in outdoor sunlight but largely absent indoors, where it’s not emitted by artificial lights and ultraviolet protective coatings on windows also filter out violet light wavelengths.
In a paper
published online May 24 in the
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
, the research team explained the molecular mechanism behind this violet light effect on myopia progression and presented a new function of the OPN5 protein. OPN5 is part of a group of photoreceptor proteins called opsins found in the membranes of cells that are not involved in forming visual images but that play other important roles in the eye.
A diagram illustrating how violet light interacts with the photoreceptor protein OPN5 to prevent progression of myopia. At top, A, a normal eye. In the middle, B, shows a myopic eye with characteristic elongation between the cornea and the retina and a thinning of the vascular layer called the choroid. The bottom, C, shows that violet suppresses the elongation and thinning of the choroid. (Illustration: Toshihide Kurihara)
The researchers used an established mouse model of myopia to demonstrate that without OPN5, violet light did nothing to halt elongation of the eye. Mice without the OPN5 protein also saw continued thinning of the choroid, a vascular layer that decreases in thickness in myopic eyes.
At Cincinnati Children’s,
Richard Lang, Ph.D.
, has played a key role in detailing unexpected roles that opsins play in the skin and the brain in addition to the eye. Some of his previous work has shown that Opsin 5  could regulate dopamine levels in the eye.
Because dopamine has a role in myopia development, he says, “it then became obvious that Opsin 5 was likely to be the light sensor that explained the observations of the Keio group — that violet light could suppress myopia. When we approached Machelle Pardue, Toshi Kurihara, and Kazuo Tsubota, they were keen to assess this question. My group has been delighted to take part in this collaboration.”
Understanding how violet light protects against worsening myopia is key as the condition’s prevalence accelerates. Already, roughly a third of people around the world are myopic, and some projections suggest nearly 5 billion people will have the condition by 2050. Nearsightedness typically begins in school-age children, and it’s often not considered a significant problem since it can be corrected with glasses. Yet, in China, myopia is the second-leading cause of blindness.
Slowing or stopping the changes in the eye that lead to myopia will limit the number of people who develop what’s called high myopia—elongation so severe that it can lead to detached retinas, glaucoma, and other problems that cause vision loss. A
2016 study in the journal
Ophthalmology
predicted nearly 10% of the world’s population will have high myopia by 2050.
“This study really does point to the fact that violet light is protective, and now there's a mechanism, this OPN5, that may underlie that,” says
Machelle Pardue, Ph.D.
, professor in the Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering at Georgia Tech and Emory and a co-author of the study. “N

• CommenterPerson引用的研究侧重于环境因素（如户外活动时间）对近视的影响，而Terr_的评论更关注光谱中特定波长的光对眼睛的潜在治疗效果及风险。
• Terr_进一步提出了实际操作中可能遇到的问题，例如如何避免紫外线对眼睛的伤害，以及蓝光在夜间对人体生物钟的干扰。
• 争议的焦点可能在于光疗法的有效性和安全性，尤其是在不同波长的光对眼睛的潜在影响方面。Terr_对具体波长的关注和对自制光源的担忧，显示了对该疗法实际应用中的谨慎态度。

总结来看，讨论围绕近视成因的环境因素和光疗法的潜在效果及风险展开，参与者提供了不同的视角和关注点。

data.title: Why ML/OCaml are good for writing compilers (1998)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了为何ML/OCaml等语言非常适合编写编译器。作者强调了以下几个关键特性：

1. **垃圾回收**：ML的垃圾回收机制高效且自动，简化了处理复杂数据结构的生命周期管理，避免了手动内存管理。
2. **尾递归优化**：ML自动优化尾递归，适合处理编译器中常见的递归数据结构，节省栈空间。
3. **数据类型匹配**：ML的数据类型（如字符串和整数）更符合编译过程的需求，且支持大数运算，避免了手动实现或绕过。
4. **类型构造器和模式匹配**：ML的类型构造器和模式匹配非常适合描述抽象语法树等结构，使代码更简洁、可读。
5. **安全性**：ML的强类型系统和不可变数据结构确保了程序的可靠性，减少了运行时错误，如段错误。

总体而言，ML/OCaml提供了强大的工具和特性，使得编写编译器变得更加高效和愉快。

44048372.article_content:
Why ML/OCaml are good for writing compilers
Why ML/OCaml are good for writing compilers
Author:
Dwight VandenBerghe
Email:
dwight@pentasoft.com
Date:
1998/07/28
Forums:
comp.compilers
Let's use the term "ML" to mean SML or Objective Caml.  I'm a devotee
of Ocaml, but I have SML/NJ installed and although I prefer the
distribution, tools and overall implementation of Ocaml, I'd be
happy to write in SML/NJ if Ocaml wasn't around.  (I can't speak
for Haskell, gofer, hugs, or any of the lazy languages.  I think
that there are different kinds of people, some of whom like things
like deferred evaluation and other who like strict call-by-value.
I'm decidedly in the latter camp; I like how clean strict evaluation
is, how easy it is to understand exactly what is going on, and I
find that I have to give a little of that up with Haskell.  But
your mileage may vary.)  So although when I am writing about "ML"
I am writing about Ocaml, what I say also applies, I think, to SML/NJ.
So here is an unordered list of language features that seems to me
to make writing compilers a pleasure rather than a horrendous chore.
1.  Garbage collection.  It may seem elementary to mention this,
but gc is an incredible boon to programs that have lots of complex
data structures with short-to-intermediate lifetimes.  And compilers
are, above all, programs with complex data structures.  You gotta
be a data structure junkie to like compilers.  Well, C/C++, Pascal,
and their ilk, with unrestricted pointers and malloc and their
cousins, make you take out your own trash.  You have to be the
programmer and the janitor, at the same time.  Some of us are
better programmers than we are janitors.  ML has, perhaps, the
best gc around; it's so fast that for many real apps it's as fast
as the C++ malloc/free, and maybe even a little faster in some
cases.  You don't have to wring your hands about using ML's gc,
as you do with Java's, which is slow.  It's just there, invisible,
blindingly fast, and it works all the time, and your life is thus
made much easier.
2.  Tail recursion is optimized.  Thus, once you know how to take
advantage of it, you can write tree walks that don't eat up stack
space, and are very fast.  Now, to be fair, there are C++ compilers
(like VisualC++ 5) that supposedly have some tail recursion
eliminated, but you can't count on it (VC has a lot of bugs in
theirs).  ML is matched to recursion very well, and since many
of the data structures in compilers tend to be best handled with
recursive procedures, there is a good fit there.
3.  The data types in ML match the compiling process.  Compilers
don't tend to worry about unsigned shorts vs signed chars,
but use "ints" everywhere, as well as strings.  Strings are used
all over the place, and C/C++ are pretty terrible with strings,
even in the presence of templates.  There are some places in
compilers where it's nice to have arithmetic on quantities a
little larger than ints, so the "bignum" facility is actually
useful in those cases (like when you have to fold constants
or tokenize with a little more precision than the underlying
numeric types, then convert back to the native form).  If you
don't have bignums, then you have to write your own, or resort
to subterfuge.  (See guru compiler writer Dave Hanson's "C
Interfaces and Implementations" for an example of what I mean.)
4.  The type constructors in ML are just plain wonderful for
describing things like ASTs (abstract syntax trees).  They
implement what are sometimes called "tagged unions" - that is,
a union data type (efficient, small) that, unlike with C/C++,
come along with a tag field that tells what's in the union.
This is enforced: in other words, there's no way to circumvent
it.  ML pattern matching is designed to work with tagged unions
so that the source code is incredibly readable, for functions
that take a data structure as an argument.  Combine this with
type inference and tail recursion elimination, and you have
a language that is optimized for recursive functions that
take complex data structures are arguments ... sound familiar?
5.  Safety.  ML was conceived as a solution to the main problem
faced by mathematicians using automated theorem provers: that
because of the type-free, dangerous, cavalier nature of the
usual language for that domain (Lisp), you could never be sure
that your program was going to work.  Of course, this could
be said about all languages, but ML was an attempt to restrict
the domain a bit, to add efficiency and safety at the same time.
ML programs can't crash the system; if it compiles, it will run,
and you won't get a segmentation fault.  You can prove certain
properties about your program, you can trust that certain kinds
of errors just plain can't happen.  For example, since lists are
immutable, and must contain elements of a single type, you don't
have to worry about screwing up a string list by putting an
integer in it by accident (as you can with Scheme and Lisp).
In fact, you can't put anything

data.title: George Wendt, best known for playing Norm on Cheers, dies aged 76
data.author: mellosouls
data.article_summary: 乔治·温德特（George Wendt），以在长寿情景喜剧《欢乐酒店》（Cheers）中饰演诺姆（Norm）而闻名的演员，于76岁去世。他出演了该剧全部275集，并获得六次艾美奖提名。温德特还曾在《辛普森一家》、《家庭 Guy》、《弗雷泽》等剧中客串同一角色。他的家人和《欢乐酒店》的联合主演们纷纷表示哀悼，特德·丹森（Ted Danson）称其为“亲爱的朋友”，而约翰·拉岑伯格（John Ratzenberger）则赞扬了他的演技。温德特也参与过电影和舞台剧，如《发胶》（Hairspray）。他的离世令许多同事和粉丝深感悲痛。

44048035.article_content:
George Wendt in Cheers, circa 1985.
Photograph: PictureLux/The Hollywood Archive/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
George Wendt in Cheers, circa 1985.
Photograph: PictureLux/The Hollywood Archive/Alamy
US television
George Wendt, best known for playing Norm on Cheers, dies aged 76
Emmy-nominated comedian and actor, best known for role in long-running sitcom, was also in Family Guy and Frasier
A man walked into a bar – and every Cheers episode, George Wendt’s Norm made it funny
Benjamin Lee
Tue 20 May 2025 16.09 EDT
Last modified on Wed 21 May 2025 01.26 EDT
Share
George Wendt, the actor best known for playing Norm in long-running sitcom Cheers, has died at 76.
His death was confirmed by his publicist in a statement.
“George was a doting family man, a well-loved friend and confidant to all of those lucky enough to have known him,” his family said in a statement. “He will be missed forever. The family has requested privacy during this time.”
A man walked into a bar – and every Cheers episode, George Wendt’s Norm made it funny
Read more
He died peacefully in his sleep at home.
Wendt starred in Cheers from 1982 to 1993, appearing in all 275 episodes of the hit sitcom. He earned six Emmy nominations for his work on the show.
“The Norm you see in Cheers has been years in the making,” Wendt
once said
of his character. “I have some characteristics in common with him besides our fondness for beer. But I think I’m a lot happier than Norm.” He also added: “I was a beer drinker long before Cheers. When I put a couple of six packs on top of my grocery shopping cart, people are pleased. I tell ‘em I’m taking them home to rehearse.”
He went on to play the character of Norm in a number of other shows including Frasier, Wings, The Simpsons, Family Guy and The Tortellis.
On Tuesday, his Cheers co-stars paid tribute, including Ted Danson, who played the barman Sam. “I am devastated to hear that Georgie is no longer with us,” he said in a statement. “I am sending all my love to Bernadette and the children. It is going to take me a long time to get used to this. I love you, Georgie.”
Rhea Perlman, who played waitress Carla Tortelli, remembered him as “the sweetest, kindest man I ever met.”
“It was impossible not to like him,” she added. “As Carla, I was often standing next to him, as Norm always took the same seat at the end of the bar, which made it easy to grab him and beat the crap out of him at least once a week. I loved doing it and he loved pretending it didn’t hurt. What a guy! I’ll miss him more than words can say.”
John Ratzenberger, who played fellow Cheers regular Cliff Clavin, said he was “heartbroken”.
“For 11 years on Cheers, we shared a stage, a lot of laughs and a front-row seat to one of television’s most beloved friendships. George brought Norm to life with a subtle brilliance — the kind that made it look easy. That was his gift,” he said in a statement.
Kelsey Grammer, who appeared in Cheers and Frasier with Wendt,
told the Hollywood Reporter:
“I believe mourning is a private matter. But I liked George a lot. He was beloved by millions.”
After Cheers, Wendt also led short-lived sitcom The George Wendt Show in 1995 which was cancelled after six episodes. His other television credits included Sabrina the Teenage Witch, Colombo, Portlandia and The Goldbergs.
His film credits included Guilty by Suspicion with Robert De Niro, Fletch with Chevy Chase, Space Truckers with Dennis Hopper and Forever Young with Mel Gibson. He also played Macaulay Culkin’s father in Michael Jackson’s Black or White video.
On stage, Wendt also starred in Hairspray on Broadway, playing Edna Turnblad. “It was one of my two favorite roles, apart from Norm,”
he said
. “Absolute utter joy and entirely different from anything in my world.”
Most recently, he appeared in a season of The Masked Singer and 2022’s festive comedy Christmas with the Campbells. He also reunited with members of the Cheers cast at the 2024 Emmys.

data.title: Violence on TV: what happens to children who watch?
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 一项由蒙特利尔大学Linda Pagani教授主导的新研究表明，学龄前男孩若暴露于暴力电视内容，十多年后在青少年中期更可能出现反社会和暴力行为。研究跟踪了近2000名出生于1997至1998年的儿童，家长报告孩子在3.5岁和4.5岁时的暴力电视观看频率，孩子在15岁时自我报告反社会行为。结果显示，只有男孩在15岁时表现出明显的反社会行为增加，如攻击、威胁、参与 gang fight 和使用武器。女孩未发现类似影响。研究强调了限制幼儿接触暴力媒体内容的必要性，并呼吁公共健康倡议以帮助家长和社区做出明智选择。研究发表于2025年1月的《国际环境研究与公共健康期刊》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：暴力内容对儿童的影响以及因果关系

不同观点：
• [tetris11] 认为，如果一味保护儿童不受任何形式的暴力影响，可能会导致他们缺乏应对现实世界挑战的能力。他以" demolition man"（毁灭者曼风格的世界）作比喻，暗示过度保护可能导致社会在面对欺凌者时更加脆弱，因为其他人没有经历过或学会如何应对暴力。

• [ars] 则对暴力内容与儿童行为之间的因果关系提出质疑。他认为报道或研究总结没有明确区分是暴力内容导致儿童行为暴力，还是暴力倾向更强的儿童倾向于选择观看更多暴力内容。他以自己观察到的男孩为例，指出有暴力倾向的孩子更喜欢观看暴力电视节目，暗示可能是孩子的性格决定了他们的媒体选择，而不是媒体内容改变了孩子的性格。

补充讨论：
• [tetris11] 的观点更侧重于社会和教育的长远影响，担心过度保护可能会导致孩子无法应对现实中的暴力情况。

• [ars] 的观点则集中在因果关系的讨论上，认为需要更多科学证据来证明暴力媒体对儿童行为的影响是直接的因果关系，而不是反过来由孩子的性格决定他们的媒体消费习惯。

• 争议的焦点在于暴力内容对儿童行为的影响究竟是直接的因果关系，还是受到儿童本身性格特质的影响。这涉及到如何解读相关研究以及如何制定相关政策来保护儿童免受潜在不良内容的影响。

44046812.article_content:
Boys exposed to violent screen content in the preschool years were more likely to become antisocial and violent themselves a decade later, in their mid-teens, a new study shows.
Linda Pagani
Credit: Amélie Philibert, Université de Montréal
Results of new study led by Linda Pagani, Professor at the Université de Montreal’s School of Psychoeducation, show long-term associated risks of early exposure to violent content in childhood and later teen antisocial behavior, more than a decade later.
“Although past evidence showing causal links between modelling and getting rewarded for violence had an immediate impact on aggressive behavior in 4-year-old children, few studies have investigated long-term risks with antisocial behavior. We studied such risks in mid-adolescence, explained Pagani, who is also a researcher at
the Centre de recherche Azrieli du CHU Sainte-Justine.
It was ideal to study this question with typically developing middle-class children because, as a population, they have the lowest chances of engaging in aggression and behavior harmful to others.”
Close to 2,000 children
In all, Pagani and her team looked at 963 girls and 982 boys born between the springs of 1997 and 1998 who were enrolled in the Quebec Longitudinal Study of Child Development. Parents reported the frequency of their child’s exposure to violent television content at ages 3.5 and 4.5 years old. Boys and girls then self-reported on several aspects of antisocial behavior at age 15.
The study defines screen violence as anything “characterized by physical aggression, verbal aggression, and relational aggression […] depicting situations that intentionally attempt or cause harm to others.” Children, the study says “are attracted to fast-paced, stimulating violent content, which often features appealing characters like superheroes who commit and are rewarded for aggressive acts, thus increasing the likelihood of exposure."
The researchers then conducted analyses to examine whether exposure to violent television content at ages 3.5 and 4.5 years predicted later antisocial behavior eleven years later.
The researcher added, “We statistically took into account alternative child and family factors that could have explained our results, to be as close as possible to the truth in the relationships we were looking at.”
Boys stand out
At age 15, for boys only, preschool violent televiewing predicted increases in antisocial behavior. Being exposed to violent content in early childhood predicted later aggressive behaviors such as hitting or beating another person, with the intention of obtaining something, stealing, with or without any apparent reason.
Risks also included threats, insults, and gang fight involvement. The use of weapons is also among the behavioral outcomes predicted by exposure to childhood television violence in this study. No effects were found for girls, which was not surprising given that boys are generally more exposed to such content.
Pagani concluded, “Our study provides compelling evidence that early childhood exposure to media violence can have serious, long-lasting consequences, particularly for boys. This underscore the urgent need for public health initiatives that targets campaigns to inform parents and communities about the long-term risks and empower them to make informed choices about young children's screen content exposure.”
The entire team of students from Université de Montréal and researchers from the United States and Italy established that, "Parents and communities can play a crucial role in limiting future problems by carefully avoiding young children's exposure to violent media content."
About the study
The article, “Prospective associations between preschool exposure to violent televiewing and externalizing behavior in middle adolescent boys and girls” was published on January 20, 2025 in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health.
Linda Pagani
, lead author of the study, is a professor at the Université de Montréal's School of Psychoeducation and a researcher at the Centre de recherche Azrieli du CHU Sainte-Justine and at the School Environment Research Group. Amélie Gilker-Beauchamp, Laurie-Anne Kosak and Kianoush Harandian are graduate students under her direction.
Claudio Longobardi
is professor in the Department of Psychology at the University of Turin, in Italy. The study’s senior author is
Eric F. Dubow
is distinguished research professor and director of clinical training in the Department of Psychology of Bowling Green State University, in Ohio.
This work was made possible thanks to the participation of parents, teachers and children in the Quebec Longitudinal Study of Child Development, and under the auspices of the Institut de la statistique du Québec for data collection, storage and hosting. data.title: Chipmaker TSMC is booming, but its factory near Portland is at a low point
data.author: rwc9
data.article_summary: 台积电（TSMC）在2024年业绩亮眼，受益于人工智能带动的半导体需求增长。然而，其位于波特兰附近的工厂TSMC Washington（前身为WaferTech）表现不佳，2024年销售额下降超过30%，出现3200万美元的亏损。该工厂使用的是25年前的技术，难以满足当前市场需求，且面临贸易壁垒和地理孤立等挑战。尽管如此，TSMC表示仍在投资该工厂，并进行工程师招聘和设备升级。相比之下，台积电在美国亚利桑那州建设了更先进的工厂，而Camas工厂因技术落后和空间有限，发展受限。

44048120.article_content:
Chipmaker TSMC is booming, but its factory near Portland is at a low point
Updated:
May. 20, 2025, 5:19 a.m.
|
Published:
May. 19, 2025, 6:02 a.m.
TSMC Washington, formerly known as WaferTech, opened in Camas in 1998. It still makes technology from that era.
TSMC photo
By
Mike Rogoway | The Oregonian/OregonLive
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. enjoyed a remarkable year in 2024, with sales up by more than a third and profits climbing even faster.
The world’s largest chipmaker is capitalizing on the rise of artificial intelligence, which is fueling enormous demand for semiconductors using TSMC’s advanced manufacturing technology — the most sophisticated in the world.
Thousands of miles from Taiwan, though, TSMC operates a relatively small factory near Portland that relies on technology that hasn’t been cutting edge in a quarter century. TSMC Washington, formerly known as WaferTech, posted its worst results in at least a dozen years.
Sales at the factory in Camas fell by more than 30% in 2024. TSMC Washington slipped into the red for the first time in many years, reporting a $32 million loss.
TSMC Washington is suffering from a cyclical downturn in demand for chips made with older technology, the same issue that has undermined aging factories Microchip Technology and Onsemi operate in nearby Gresham.
But TSMC Washington is also coping with trade headwinds and baggage associated with its isolation, far from its corporate parent or sibling factories.
TSMC declined to comment on the financial results of its Camas factory, known in the industry as a fab, or the facility’s long-term future. But the company said it’s still investing in the site, which employs about 1,000.
“TSMC Washington is hiring engineers in Camas and upgrading some of its fab systems,” the company said in a written statement.
TSMC is a contract manufacturer, or foundry in the semiconductor industry’s parlance. It doesn’t design chips. Instead, TSMC offers leading-edge production technology to clients including Nvidia, Apple and even Intel — which began outsourcing some of its most advanced chips after because of mounting production troubles in Intel’s own fabs.
The Camas fab was TSMC’s first in the U.S. when it opened as WaferTech in 1998. Washington economic development officials hoped it would be the first of several fabs on the site east of Vancouver.
WaferTech ran into immediate problems, though, as TSMC struggled to adapt to U.S. regulations and labor practices.
“Initially it was chaos. It was just a series of ugly surprises because, when we first went in, we really expected the costs to be comparable to Taiwan. And that was extremely naive,” said Morris Chang, TSMC’s legendary founder,
in 2022
. He said the 1,000 workers in Camas cost 50% more than they would in Taiwan.
WaferTech was among the last generation of fabs to use 200-millimeter silicon wafers. The industry was on the cusp of moving to the larger, more efficient 300-millimeter standard. It’s very expensive to upgrade an older fab to larger wafers, and TSMC never did so in Camas.
“At one point that fab was doing reasonably well but you know, Morris Chang never liked it. He always felt like the world was twisting his arm to put a fab there,” said Dan Hutcheson, vice chair of the semiconductor industry research firm TechInsights.
Disheartened by its early setbacks, TSMC didn’t build any more fabs in Camas and hasn’t significantly upgraded the original one. That left it a single, secluded factory operating on its own with antiquated technology.
TSMC dropped the WaferTech name in 2023
, rebranding the site as TSMC Washington.
The Camas fab can manufacture chips with features between 0.35 microns to 0.16 microns, according to TSMC. That’s technology from around the turn of the century, the time the fab opened.
Such trailing-edge technology still has many uses, in industrial equipment, autos, appliances and the defense industry. A shortage of such chips during the pandemic pushed TSMC Washington’s sales to record highs in 2022, but now there’s a glut and the whole industry is struggling.
TSMC Washington faces other hurdles, according to Hutcheson. He said protectionist policies in China that predate the Trump administration’s trade war have made it more difficult for low-end chips made in the U.S. to find customers in Asia.
Perhaps most seriously, TSMC Washington is a small factory far removed from its parent company’s other sites. That’s a long-term problem because TSMC has long emphasized the value of operating large clusters of factories. The Camas site has only 260 acres total – a quarter of the space that advanced fabs now seek.
Over the past several years, TSMC has built a leading-edge factory on 1,000-acres in Arizona and plans at least two more there. It has left Camas alone.
Despite last year’s sharp downturn, TSMC Washington doesn’t appear to have endured the mass layoffs that Microchip Technology and Onsemi have undertaken this year as demand for older-generation chips

data.title: Overview of the Ada Computer Language Competition (1979)
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ada语言的设计背景及其在安全关键嵌入式系统中的应用

不同观点：
• [askvictor] 提到他们在工作中讨论了Ada，并研究其是否是用于安全关键嵌入式系统的最佳语言，暗示Ada可能是该领域的有力候选者。

• [kevlar700] 指出Co-Pilot错误地描述Ada是由委员会设计的，而实际上Ada是通过多个竞争过程产生的。这表明Ada的设计过程比通常理解的更为复杂和竞争性。

• [synack] 提供了有关语言提案及其优点的详细信息，分享了一个非常大的PDF文件链接（https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/trecms/pdf/ADB950587.pdf），为讨论提供了更深入的技术背景支持。

• [jakeisnotadog1] 仅提供了一个存档链接（https://archive.is/hZcMO），没有进一步的评论，可能意在提供额外的参考资料。

补充讨论：
• Ada的设计过程是讨论的一个焦点，[kevlar700] 特别指出了对Ada的常见误解，并试图澄清其设计并非简单的委员会产物，而是经过多个竞争过程。

• 提供了技术文档和参考链接（[synack] 和 [jakeisnotadog1]），为深入理解Ada的语言设计和其应用场景提供了更多资源。

• 争议的焦点似乎在于Ada设计过程的准确描述及其在安全关键系统中的适用性，[askvictor] 的工作讨论可能反映了对Ada实际应用效果的现实考量。

data.title: Withnail and I (2001)
data.author: dcminter
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕电影《Withnail & I》的各种观点和评论，包括电影的风格、情节、影响以及个人联想。

不同观点：
• 电影的语言和台词非常经典，令人印象深刻，例如 "Balls. We want the finest wines available to humanity..." 等台词被频繁引用，显示出观众对电影台词的喜爱 ([cccybernetic])。
• 部分观众认为电影带有忧郁的暗流，尽管整体上是滑稽的，这体现了电影在情感层次上的复杂性 ([bilekas])。
• 有人认为电影没有明确的叙事结构，更像是生活片段的拼接，类似于《Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas》，强调了其“生活切片”式的风格 ([BLKNSLVR])。
• 有评论将《Withnail & I》与其他电影或电视剧进行比较，如《Naked》和《The Young Ones》，指出其在幽默和哲学深度上的独特性，同时也指出了类似作品的联系和区别 ([hounddogX], [macleginn])。

补充讨论：
• 电影的拍摄地点和背景引起了讨论，例如有观众提到电影中的Camden镇至今仍有类似的场景和人物，增加了电影的真实感和代入感 ([gilleain])。
• 一些观众分享了他们对电影角色的个人联想和回忆，例如有观众提到自己认识的某人像电影中的Vivian，以及电影中角色的性格在现实中的投射 ([polyvisual], [fennecbutt])。
• 部分评论提供了观看资源和相关视频链接，如与导演Bruce Robinson的观看活动和相关视频片段，为其他观众提供了更多的参考和观影体验 ([emmelaich], [herbturbo])。
• 争议的焦点可能在于电影的理解和评价上，有些观众初次观看时未能完全理解电影的内涵，但随着更多的背景知识和重看，逐渐体会到电影的深度和魅力 ([BLKNSLVR])。

总体而言，观众对《Withnail & I》的评价多为正面，强调了其经典台词、情感深度以及与其他类似作品的比较和联系。同时，电影的背景和拍摄地点也引发了观众的共鸣和回忆。

data.title: The Future of Junior Software Engineering Roles
data.author: pootietangus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对软件工程职业发展的影响，特别是对初级和高级工程师角色的影响

不同观点：
• **ochronus**：认为初级工程师在合适的条件下能迅速成长为中级工程师，而行业依赖于大量中级工程师来维持团队的“速度”。如果转向“高级工程师+AI代理”的模式，公司将难以形成新团队，因为高级工程师退休后没有足够的中级工程师接替。此外，AI目前停留在初级水平，需要高级工程师花费大量时间修正其输出。

• **marcus_holmes**：回顾自己早年入行经历，认为未来自学编程者将增多，AI会淘汰初级角色。但总有人会因兴趣继续编程，而那些仅因职业前景入行的人可能会离开。

• **zkmon**：认为软件工作不仅仅是编码，特别是在非科技公司，编码只占工作的10%。AI不会取代初级工程师角色，因为这些角色承担了大量繁琐的工作，并且用于分担风险和责任。实际工作多由非员工的咨询顾问完成。

• **dzonga**：指出计算机科学课程更多关注理论和数学，编程实践较少，这可能导致毕业生在进入职场时缺乏实际编程技能。

• **kazinator**：质疑所谓高级工程师只指挥而不实际编码的组织是否存在，认为这种描述不现实。

• **ggm**：强调毕业后12-18个月的实际工作经验至关重要，认为如果当时有行业实习，自己的职业发展会更好。

• **codr7**：提出有远见的公司可以雇佣、培训初级工程师并外派盈利，这是一种商业模式。

• **constantcrying**：认为计算机科学教育的核心是抽象问题解决能力，而非具体编程语言或工具。

• **rvz**：认为AI在网页开发领域已达到高级工程师水平，未来这类开发者的职业前景黯淡。

• **tropicalfruit**：幽默地预测未来所有人都将成为初级，能够独立思考将成为超能力。

• **pootietangus**：质疑如果高级工程师能将问题分解并交由AI完成，那么是否还有必要保留初级工程师。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：AI是否会取代初级工程师，以及这种转变对软件团队构成的长期影响。有人认为AI目前能力有限，需要高级工程师修正；有人则认为AI将迅速取代初级甚至高级角色。
• **教育与实践的脱节**：讨论中提到计算机科学教育中理论与实践的脱节，以及实习经验对职业初期发展的重要性。
• **职业发展路径**：对初级工程师成长为中级、高级工程师的路径及其在行业中的重要性存在不同看法，特别是在AI参与越来越多的情况下如何维持团队的“速度”和知识传承。

data.title: Life before the web – Running a Startup in the 1980's (2016)
data.author: gscott
data.article_summary: 本文是Robert Gaskins的系列故事的第二部分，他于1984年在Forethought Inc.参与发明了PowerPoint，这是微软的首次重大收购。Gaskins回顾了1980年代创办初创企业的挑战，当时没有互联网，需提前长远规划并准确预测市场。与当今轻量级、快速迭代的网络产品开发不同，那时需要大量前期投资才能获得反馈或销售。PowerPoint最初为Mac开发，尽管Windows宣布在先，但其推出延迟，使得PowerPoint在1990年成为首个主要的Windows演示应用程序，并迅速成为国际标准。Gaskins的团队在1984年至1987年间多次面临清算风险，但最终成功将PowerPoint年销售额增长至1亿美元，并在1993年退休。
data.comments_summary:
