44013046.article_content:
This is
part two
of a series of stories by
Robert Gaskins
who helped invent PowerPoint at Forethought Inc. in 1984 (
read part one here
). It was the first significant acquisition made by Microsoft.
We spoke to Robert about building a startup in the 1980s and what life was like negotiating with, and working for Microsoft. After the sale Robert reported directly to Bill Gates, heading up Microsoft’s business unit in Silicon Valley. He managed the growth of PowerPoint to
$100 million in annual sales
before his retirement in 1993.
This post looks at
what it was like running a startup in the 1980’s
and the differences Gaskins and his team experienced back then compared to running a startup today.
Here’s Gaskins in his own words …
A different age
An early mock-up of a PowerPoint slide
Developing PowerPoint in the 1980s was so incredibly different that a description of how we worked in the mid-1980s doesn’t seem to make any sense, unless one remembers that the Internet was completely unknown outside a small research community in 1984.
I had access to an ARPAnet connection when I worked at the Bell-
Northern Research laboratory in Palo Alto in the late 1970s, but I had no real experience
with it—it wasn’t something we used every day. Lots of things about the way both startups and larger software companies worked prior to the web don’t make any sense in the current age.
A software startup in the 1980s was a more difficult problem. You had to plan ahead a great distance and “call the shot” accurately, since a considerable investment was required before much in the way of feedback, let alone sales, could be available.
Today it’s the fashion to make web services in a very “lightweight” way, to offer minimally viable web products free, and to iterate rapidly as experience is gained with initial web users. Without the web, none of that was possible.
The competition
As a startup you can get crushed by a 100 pound gorilla before you even realise it sat on you. You have to be nimble enough to avoid that whatever era you are working in, whether that’s the 1980s, or 2016. Twenty years after we started developing PowerPoint Paul Graham
famously said
:
The best way to solve a problem is often to redefine it
This was a path we followed at the time. We certainly had a lot of competitors who were making presentation software for MSDOS PCs and for Apple IIs—that is, for the old command-line operating systems. I drew up a table of competitors with such products, and there were more than 30 of them, mostly selling for between $300 and $700 a copy (in 1983 !) But PowerPoint wouldn’t run on those machines.
The real competitors would be whichever successful, big software companies from that world would first make the jump to Mac and Windows. Mac had early enthusiasts, but it remained underpowered for a long time and wasn’t so attractive to businesses using MS-DOS PCs. Windows—or, at least, something like Mac’s graphical platform delivered for machines that were open and less expensive—was what customers were waiting for.
We were “writing off the entire installed base of PCs,” betting that Windows and Macintosh would grow to dominance. So these existing products were not the problem.
Windows was announced at Comdex in Fall 1983, before Mac shipped. It was much slower in shipping than anyone expected, so we redirected our first version to Mac, but when PowerPoint for Mac shipped in 1987 I thought we could  ship a Windows version in 1988. I turned out to be wrong: we didn’t ship the first PowerPoint for Windows until 1990, two years later than planned! By then we had very large competitors from the MS-DOS world, with massive numbers of users, who had only to ship a Windows version to take their users with them. Largest of all (over half the total market) was Harvard Graphics from Software Publishing Corporation (SPC).
There was also Freelance from Lotus Development, popular because it interworked with the Lotus 1–2–3 spreadsheet. WordPerfect was developing a presentation product to go with its market-leading MS-DOS word processor. People in the publishing industry liked Persuasion from Aldus which was a Mac product, but was moving to Windows as rapidly as possible.
But, as it turned out, PowerPoint was the first major presentation application for Windows, and it shipped in 1990 on the same day as the first adequate version of Windows—Bill Gates could and did use PowerPoint to announce Windows 3.0. Freelance and Persuasion shipped on Windows about one year later; Harvard Graphics shipped on Windows about two years later; and the WordPerfect product never really appeared on Windows in timely fashion. A year or two is an eternity in a rapidly exploding market; PowerPoint on Windows immediately became the international standard, and has defended that position for 25 years.
A rocky road
From mid-1984 to mid-1987, we faced the very real prospect of liquidation at least every six months. For three Christmases in a row, we took off a week for the
44013046.article_summary: 本文是Robert Gaskins的系列故事的第二部分，他于1984年在Forethought Inc.参与发明了PowerPoint，这是微软的首次重大收购。Gaskins回顾了1980年代创办初创企业的挑战，当时没有互联网，需提前长远规划并准确预测市场。与当今轻量级、快速迭代的网络产品开发不同，那时需要大量前期投资才能获得反馈或销售。PowerPoint最初为Mac开发，尽管Windows宣布在先，但其推出延迟，使得PowerPoint在1990年成为首个主要的Windows演示应用程序，并迅速成为国际标准。Gaskins的团队在1984年至1987年间多次面临清算风险，但最终成功将PowerPoint年销售额增长至1亿美元，并在1993年退休。

data.title: Proposal for Standardized JSX
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: 文章提出对JSX进行标准化，指出当前基于导入的JSX转换方案不适合标准化，因为存在路径不统一、缺乏工具支持、无法在一个文件中使用多个实现等问题。文章提出一个简单的方案：将JSX表达式转换为普通的JavaScript对象字面量，标签置于`Symbol.for("JSX")`下，所有子元素放在"children"字段中，其他属性保持不变。此方案具有简单、无需全局变量或自动导入、支持框架互操作等优点，并且易于实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JSX的标准化和实用性

不同观点：
• [elehack] 认为在主流框架之外使用JSX比较麻烦，并因此开发了自己的库（Hyperstatic）。他对JSX的潜在标准化表示兴趣，认为这可能减少对类似库的需求。
• [orta] 提到了在TC39中有关"ESX"标准化的讨论，并提供了相关链接，表明对JSX标准化的关注和参与。
• [pwdisswordfishz] 持怀疑态度，认为没有推动JSX标准化的实际努力，并暗示Facebook的JSX文档可能不具备实质性内容。
• [silverwind] 希望未来标准能允许在表达式上下文中使用多个元素，而不需要使用碎片（fragments）或数组，以此改善当前的语法。
• [aatd86] 认为React选择JSX元素语法并不意味着它应该被标准化，暗示JSX可能只是React特定需求的结果，而非普遍标准。
• [90s_dev] 支持JSX的标准化，并介绍了自己的提案，将JSX转换为一种自包含的、通用的结构，不依赖于导入或全局变量，同时提供了使用案例和具体实现。
• [gherkinnn] 表达了对非JSX模板语言的不满，认为JSX在模板编写中具有优势，暗示JSX的实用性和用户体验优于其他模板语言。
• [palmfacehn] 对JSX持中立或略微消极的态度，表示满足于使用<template>元素，并偏好HTML、CSS和原生JS的组合，暗示对抽象的偏好。

补充讨论：
- JSX标准化进程中的具体技术方案和提案（如[90s_dev]的提案）是讨论的一个重要方面。
- 不同开发者对JSX的需求和使用场景各异，反映出JSX在不同项目和环境中的适应性。
- 争议的焦点在于JSX是否应被标准化，以及标准化的具体形式和必要性。
- 对JSX的偏好和实用性评价因开发者的经验和项目需求而异。

44047976.article_content:
Proposal for standardized JSX
There has been no push for JSX standardization.
Partly this seems to be because everyone is fine with status quo.
But JSX has proven immensely practical and
will
eventually be standardized.
Current JSX transformations are bad
It's obvious why the initial global-based solution is bad, so I won't go into that.
But the import-based solution is equally unfit for standardization:
What path should it use?
How would it work without tooling?
It doesn't allow multiple implementations per file.
The status quo for JSX assumes tooling, and inherently forfeits a path to standardization.
Simple Proposal
JSX expressions are transformed into JS object literal expressions:
Tag is placed under
Symbol.for("JSX")
.
All children are placed in a
"children"
field.
All other properties remain as-is.
Live Demo
Best viewed on desktop
Babel implementation
Benefits
Extremely simple
Plain JS objects
No globals
No auto-imports
No pragmas
Supports framework interop
Easy to implement

data.title: What are people doing? Live-ish estimates based on global population dynamics
data.author: willbc
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要展示了全球人口动态的实时数据。页面显示当前全球人口总数为0，估计每秒出生人数和死亡人数均为0，每秒人口净增长也为0。同时，页面提供了协调世界时（UTC）和在线观看人数。下方可能还包含更详细的分类活动数据。这些信息旨在提供全球人口变化的实时概览。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个展示实时数据的仪表盘项目的功能、数据准确性、统计数据的意义以及某些统计项的数值进行了讨论。

不同观点：
• [Aardwolf] 认为项目错过了一个加入“当前查看此仪表盘人数 (0.00000125%)”统计的机会，因为项目已经有了实时观众计数器。
• [sinuhe69] 提到了另一个由DataFlow制作的、关于美国日常活动的可视化项目，并认为其更具吸引力和易理解性，尽管仅基于美国数据。
• [alwa] 引用更新日志中关于“亲密关系次数总是偶数”的修复，幽默地提到FTX事件，并对项目的质量表示赞赏。
• [satellite2] 对亲密关系和战争的数量几乎相同表示悲哀，但也对项目表示赞赏。
• [perilunar] 提出希望加入的其他统计数据，如在空中、太空中和海上的人数，并提供了相关网站的参考。
• [avvt4avaw] 质疑出生和死亡人数每秒的计数器数值频繁波动，认为这不合理。
• [bspammer] 幽默地建议将“实时观众”计数器作为一个实际条目放在页面底部。
• [hnaccountme] 对亲密关系和战争有相同的数字表示滑稽。
• [bvirb] 观察到洗手间使用次数增加了一次，表示数据准确。
• [randomstate] 对亲密关系和战争有相同数字表示困惑。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 认为统计数据没有反映出其养育子女时间比父母多20倍的现实情况，并提到全球出生率和戒烟趋势。
• [ggm] 对出生率和死亡率之间的差距表示惊讶，认为与全球出生率下降的趋势不符，并提到非洲的高出生率对全球人口的影响。
• [wanderingstan] 对每秒两人去世的统计感到震撼，认为这让人意识到生命的短暂，并赞扬了网站的实时数据显示方式。
• [ta1243] 幽默地表示亲密关系次数高于战争次数，支持“要做爱不要战争”的理念。
• [fredski42] 认为人口增长完全归因于非洲的高出生率，并提供了维基百科关于总生育率的链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是亲密关系和战争次数相同是否合理，部分用户对此表示困惑或幽默，而其他用户则以此为幽默点。
- 另一个讨论点是数据的实时波动性，特别是出生和死亡人数的计数器，一些用户质疑其波动是否真实。
- 用户还提出了对项目添加额外统计数据的建议，如在空中、太空中和海上的人数，以增加项目的丰富性。
- 非洲的高出生率对全球人口增长的影响也被提及，并提供了外部链接以供参考。

• [alwa] 引用更新日志中关于“亲密关系次数总是偶数”的修复，幽默地提到FTX事件，并对项目的质量表示赞赏。
• [satellite2] 对亲密关系和战争的数量几乎相同表示悲哀，但也对项目表示赞赏。
• [perilunar] 提出希望加入的其他统计数据，如在空中、太空中和海上的人数，并提供了相关网站的参考。
• [avvt4avaw] 质疑出生和死亡人数每秒的计数器数值频繁波动，认为这不合理。
• [bspammer] 幽默地建议将“实时观众”计数器作为一个实际条目放在页面底部。
• [hnaccountme] 对亲密关系和战争有相同的数字表示滑稽。
• [bvirb] 观察到洗手间使用次数增加了一次，表示数据准确。
• [randomstate] 对亲密关系和战争有相同数字表示困惑。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 认为统计数据没有反映出其养育子女时间比父母多20倍的现实情况，并提到全球出生率和戒烟趋势。
• [ggm] 对出生率和死亡率之间的差距表示惊讶，认为与全球出生率下降的趋势不符，并提到非洲的高出生率对全球人口的影响。
• [wanderingstan] 对每秒两人去世的统计感到震撼，认为这让人意识到生命的短暂，并赞扬了网站的实时数据显示方式。
• [ta1243] 幽默地表示亲密关系次数高于战争次数，支持“要做爱不要战争”的理念。
• [fredski42] 认为人口增长完全归因于非洲的高出生率，并提供了维基百科关于总生育率的链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是亲密关系和战争次数相同是否合理，部分用户对此表示困惑或幽默，而其他用户则以此为幽默点。
- 另一个讨论点是数据的实时波动性，特别是出生和死亡人数的计数器，一些用户质疑其波动是否真实。
- 用户还提出了对项目添加额外统计数据的建议，如在空中、太空中和海上的人数，以增加项目的丰富性。
- 非洲的高出生率对全球人口增长的影响也被提及，并提供了外部链接以供参考。

data.title: Making video games (without an engine) in 2025
data.author: selvan
data.article_summary: 本文作者Noel Berry分享了他在2025年不使用商业游戏引擎制作游戏的经历和观点。他解释说，自己不依赖Unity或Unreal等大型引擎，而是开发自定义的小型工具和系统。Berry认为，这样可以更好地控制开发过程，避免引擎更新导致的问题，并且更符合个人和团队需求。他主要使用C#编程语言，认为其性能和语法在2025年已大幅改进，适合快速运行和日常开发。同时，C#的易用性使得团队中的多面手能够轻松上手。Berry强调，不使用引擎并不意味着从零开始一切，借助开源框架和库可以简化开发过程，并以自己与兄弟合作开发《City of None》为例，展示了小型团队如何有效利用这种方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏引擎开发与使用之间的权衡，特别是自定义引擎与使用现成引擎（如Unity、Unreal）的利弊。

不同观点：
• samiv认为，开发游戏引擎本身相对简单，真正的难点在于引擎周围的工具链和资源管道，比如数据导入、编辑器功能、数据打包等。他指出，游戏工作室通常有小型团队开发引擎，而大量工具程序员处理其他关键工作。
• JKCalhoun分享了自己的经验，使用简单的工具（如SDL2和C++）创建了一个类似辅助自行车的简单引擎。他批评高层次引擎可能会让开发者围绕引擎设计游戏，而不是根据游戏需求选择工具。
• oliverdzedou指出，学习Unreal或Unity也需要大量时间，而一旦掌握，可以节省时间。他强调，自定义引擎在处理独特和细分游戏时有优势，但并不适合所有类型游戏，比如超现实开放世界RPG。
• danielbarla同意不需要“全功能”引擎来开发简单游戏，但也指出引擎在处理复杂功能（如反向动力学和动画混合）时提供了很大帮助。
• msephton使用Lua和Love2D开发游戏，认为自定义约束可以激发创造力，并分享了自己小游戏进入最佳游戏榜单的经历。
• throwawayffffas抱怨主流引擎（如Godot、Unity、Unreal）往往预设了游戏模式，导致开发者需要大量修改和绕过预设配置。
• kkukshtel正在开发自己的C#游戏框架，认为现代C#提供了强大的功能，如跨平台开发和原生热重载，并提倡小团队和微服务架构。
• z3t4喜欢从零开始开发软件项目，认为这样可以在后期加速新功能实现，但需要多年试错才能掌握合适的架构和语言细节。
• doawoo认为，如果开发者没有明确游戏目标，自定义引擎可能导致工具闲置；而有明确游戏目标时，自定义引擎可以精确满足需求，并为后续项目提供可重用代码。
• leonard-somero不使用Unity或Unreal，但使用框架处理低层架构，自己编写游戏逻辑，以保持对游戏运作的完全控制。
• gr4vityWall关注现代.NET的热重载功能，认为这是时间节省利器，并讨论了理想引擎在快速迭代和窗口管理方面的特性。
• Lichtso指出，许多经典游戏使用自定义引擎，认为在打磨精品游戏时，自定义引擎投资可能有回报，但警告新手应避免一开始就开发引擎。
• enbugger将游戏引擎视为艺术工具，认为每个引擎都有需要学习的技巧和窍门，程序员往往对没有专用UI的工具存在偏见。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于自定义引擎与现成引擎的效率和适用性。一些开发者认为自定义引擎可以提供更大控制和独特性，而另一些开发者则强调主流引擎在处理复杂功能和快速原型设计中的优势。
• 工具链和资源管道的复杂性被认为是开发引擎的重要组成部分，往往被忽视。
• 小团队和微服务架构被提倡为加速开发和保持灵活性的有效方法。
• 热重载和快速迭代功能被认为是理想引擎的重要特性，可以显著提高开发效率。

44038209.article_content:
Noel Berry
Making Video Games in 2025 (without an engine)
May 18, 2025
It's 2025 and I am still making video games, which
according to archive.org
is 20 years since I started making games! That's a pretty long time to be doing one thing...
Screenshot of my website circa 2011
When I share stuff I'm working on, people frequently ask how I make games and are often surprised (and sometimes concerned?) when I tell them I don't use commercial game engines. There's an assumption around making games without a big tool like Unity or Unreal that you're out there hand writing your own assembly instruction by instruction.
I genuinely believe making games without a big "do everything" engine can be easier, more fun, and often less overhead. I am not making a "do everything" game and I do not need 90% of the features these engines provide. I am very particular about how my games feel and look, and how I interact with my tools. I often find the default feature implementations in large engines like Unity so lacking I end up writing my own anyway. Eventually, my projects end up being mostly my own tools and systems, and the engine becomes just a vehicle for a nice UI and some rendering...
At which point, why am I using this engine? What is it providing me? Why am I letting a tool potentially destroy my ability to work when they suddenly make
unethical and terrible business decisions
? Or push out an update that they require to run my game on consoles, that also happens to break an entire system in my game, forcing me to rewrite it? Why am I fighting this thing daily for what essentially becomes a glorified asset loader and editor UI framework, by the time I'm done working around their default systems?
The obvious answer for me is to just not use big game engines, and write my own small tools for my specific use cases. It's more fun, and I like controlling my development stack. I know when something goes wrong I can find the problem and address it, instead of submitting a bug report and 3 months later hearing back it "won't be fixed". I like knowing that in another two decades from now I will still be able to compile my game without needing to pirate an ancient version of a broken game engine.
Obviously this is my personal preference - and it's one of someone who has been making indie games for a long time. I used engines like Game Maker for years before transitioning to more lightweight and custom workflows. I also work in very small teams, where it's easy to make one-off tools for team members. But I want to push back that making games "from scratch" is some big impossible task - especially in 2025 with the state of open source frameworks and libraries. A
lot of
popular
indie
games
are made
in small
frameworks like FNA, Love2D, or SDL. Making games "without an engine" doesn't literally mean opening a plain text editor and writing system calls (unless you want to). Often, the overhead of learning how to implement these systems yourself is just as time consuming as learning the proprietary workflows of the engine itself.
With that all said, I think it'd be fun to talk about my workflow, and what I actually use to make games.
Programming Languages
Most of my career I've worked in C#, and aside from a
short stint in C++
a few years ago, I've settled back into a modern C# workflow.
I think sometimes when I mention C# to non-indie game devs their minds jump to what it looked like circa 2003 - a closed source, interpreted, verbose, garbage collected language, and... the language has
greatly
improved since then. The C# of 2025 is vastly different from the C# of even 2015, and many of those changes are geared towards the performance and syntax of the langauge. You can allocate dynamically sized arrays on the stack!
C++
can't do that (
although
C99
can ;) ...
).
The dotnet developers have also implemented hot reload in C# (which works...
most of the time
), and it's pretty fantastic for game development. You can launch your project with
dotnet watch
and it will live-update code changes, which is amazing when you want to change how something draws or the way an enemy updates.
C# also ends up being a great middle-ground between running things fast (which you need for video games) and easy to work with on a day-to-day basis. For example, I have been working on
City of None
with my brother
Liam
, who had done very little coding when we started the project. But over the last year he's slowly picked up the language to the point where he's programming entire boss fights by himself, because C# is just that accessible - and fairly foot-gun free. For small teams where everyone wears many hats, it's a really nice language.
A boss fight that Liam coded
And finally, it has built in reflection... And while I wouldn't use it for release code, being able to quickly reflect on game objects for editor tooling is very nice. I can easily make live-inspection tools that show me the state of game objects without needing any custom meta programming or in-

data.title: DDoSecrets publishes 410 GB of heap dumps, hacked from TeleMessage
data.author: micahflee
data.article_summary: 分布式秘密（DDoSecrets）发布了410 GB从以色列公司TeleMessage窃取的数据，该公司开发修改版的Signal、WhatsApp、Telegram和WeChat，用于集中存档消息。由于数据包含敏感的个人信息，DDoSecrets仅与记者和研究人员分享。事件 timeline 包括：3月，前国家安全顾问Mike Waltz被发现使用Signal群组讨论机密信息，导致国会听证；5月1日，Waltz被拍到使用TeleMessage的TM SGNL（Signal修改版）；5月3日，其源代码被发布到GitHub；5月4日和5日，TeleMessage两次被黑客攻击。分析显示，TeleMessage的产品并未如其声称的那样支持端到端加密。5月18日，其服务器漏洞细节被披露。任何访问特定URL的人都可以下载包含明文聊天记录的Java堆转储。DDoSecrets发布的这些数据揭示了TeleMessage在安全和隐私方面的严重问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TeleMessage数据泄露事件及其引发的多方讨论

不同观点：
• Aurornis认为，尽管该组织提供了访问接口，但他们并未真正“发布”任何内容，且夸大了410GB堆 dumps的数据量以吸引关注。
• Gregorvand对TeleMessage CEO的LinkedIn简介进行讽刺，质疑其领导能力和公司声誉。
• Greyface-指出Signal基金会对此次泄露事件保持沉默，与其对开源项目的强硬态度形成对比。
• Namdnay强调TeleMessage不仅有不合规的Signal分支，还涉及非法销售破解的WhatsApp，且有政府和企业购买。
• Jfritsch1984对该公司在处理敏感通信服务中的低级错误表示震惊，并质疑其合法性。
• LubesGordi解释了“heapdump”的技术含义，并质疑为何这些堆dumps会在开放的HTTP端点上出现。
• Willmarquis批评暴露未经验证的/heapdump端点是新手错误，尤其对于处理敏感政府通信的服务。

This morning, Distributed Denial of Secrets
published
410 GB of data hacked from TeleMessage, the Israeli firm that makes modified versions of Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, and WeChat that centrally archive messages. Because the data is sensitive and full of PII, DDoSecrets is only sharing it with journalists and researchers.
There's a lot of background, so here's a quick timeline of events with relevant links:
March: Then-national security advisor Mike Waltz
invited
a journalist into a Signal group where they planned
war crimes
. This led to Congressional
hearings
about Trump officials using Signal groups to discuss classified information.
May 1: Waltz (the day he was demoted from position of national security advisor) was photographed using TM SGNL, a modified version of Signal made by TeleMessage. He had texts up with Tusli Gabbard, JD Vance, and Marco Rubio.
May 3: I
published
the source code of the TM SGNL to GitHub.
May 4: TeleMessage got hacked, which I
reported
in 404 Media with Joseph Cox.
May 5: TeleMessage got hacked again by someone else, as NBC News
reported
.
May 6: I
published analysis
of the TM SGNL source code, along with some of the hacked data, that prove the TeleMessage lied about its products supporting end-to-end encryption.
May 18: I
published details
about the TeleMessage server's vulnerability in WIRED.
TLDR: if anyone on the internet loaded the URL
archive.telemessage.com/management/heapdump
, they would download a Java heap dump from TeleMessage's archive server, containing plaintext chat logs, among other things.
Now, DDoSecrets has published 410 GB of these TeleMessage heap dumps. Here's the DDoSecrets description of
the release
:
Thousands of heap dumps taken May 4, 2025 from TeleMessage, which produces software used to archive encrypted messaging apps such as Signal and WhatsApp. The service came to public notice in 2025 when it was reported that former national security adviser Mike Waltz used TeleMessage while communicating with members of the Trump administration, including Vice President JD Vance and Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. TeleMessage has been used by the federal government since at least February 2023.
Some of the archived data includes plaintext messages while other portions only include metadata, including sender and recipient information, timestamps, and group names. To facilitate research, Distributed Denial of Secrets has extracted the text from the original heap dumps.
It seems that the SignalGate saga of staggering incompetence is not yet complete. I'm digging into this data right now. It's bonkers.
Note: I'm a member of the DDoSecrets collective. If you can,
donate
! DDoSecrets operates on a shoestring budget and does incredibly impactful work.

data.article_summary: 文章由物理学家Nick McGreivy撰写，讲述了他对AI加速科学研究的期望与实际经历之间的落差。最初，他受AI高薪和潜力的吸引，尝试将AI应用于等离子物理研究，尤其是用AI解决偏微分方程（PDEs）。然而，他发现许多声称AI比传统数值方法快数百万倍的研究结果存在夸大，且存在数据泄漏等问题。最终，他质疑AI是否真能如宣传那样“加速”或“革命性”地推动科学发现。尽管AI在科学领域的应用迅速增加，但作者认为，AI的成功往往被过度乐观地宣传，且其在科学中的实际影响可能被夸大。他提醒，不应过分依赖单一研究范式，而需谨慎评估AI的真正潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI（特别是AI在科学研究中）的 hype（过度宣传）和实际效果的争议

不同观点：
• **对AI过度宣传的担忧**：[shantnutiwari] 担心当前对AI的批评可能在未来被证明是错误的，因为如果未来AI找到实际应用场景，现在的批评者可能会被认为是“卢德分子”（反对技术进步的人）。这种担忧反映了在不确定的未来面前，对当前批评的谨慎态度。

• **对AI研究中的激励机制的讨论**：[raesene9] 指出，AI作为一种新技术可能获得超出其实际价值的关注，特别是在科学研究中，研究人员的激励机制（如追求正面结果）可能误导公众。该评论强调了理解人们动机的必要性。

• **学术问题的重复**：[rhubarbtree] 认为AI领域的问题只是学术界普遍问题的重复，如追求引用量和职业发展，而非追求真理。AI只是这一现象的又一个例子。

• **AI实际应用的局限性**：[angry_moose] 分享了在AI结构求解器方面的实际经验，指出AI在处理非线性问题时表现不佳，暗示当前AI技术在实际工程应用中仍有限。

• **AI对效率的提升**：[Flamentono2] 强调AI在提高研究人员工作效率方面的实际应用，例如代码生成和图像处理，认为尽管存在 hype，AI确实带来了新的变革，特别是在数据处理和反馈机制方面。

• **AI研究的可重复性和模型更新问题**：[sublimefire] 指出AI研究中的结果难以重复验证，尤其是新模型和训练数据的快速变化使得研究结果的普遍性和适用性难以确定。

• **AI驱动 breakthrough（突破）的质疑**：[plasticeagle] 质疑AI是否真的带来了任何领域的重大突破或渐进式改进，认为目前的AI可能只是在 remix（重新混合）已有知识，而非创造新知识。

• **对AI批评的正常化视角**：[shalmanese] 认为文章中提到的现象只是学术界长期问题的自然延伸，学术论文是复杂社会技术系统的产物，需要读者具备“阅读”学术声明的能力。

• **AI公司和市场的动机**：[wrren] 指出AI公司有强烈的动机展示其模型的超人智能，即便夸大其实际能力。这类宣传往往受到商业利益驱动，而批评文章则缺乏同样的市场影响力。

补充讨论：
• **标题更改的疑问**：[-__---____-ZXyw] 对文章标题是否更改提出了疑问，反映了读者对信息传播过程中可能出现的不一致性的关注。

• **对AI winter（寒冬）的预测**：[nicoco] 提到学术出版行业普遍存在的问题（如负结果不发表、过度宣传）同样适用于AI领域，并预测AI可能即将进入寒冬期。

• **跨领域合作的重要性**：[ausbah] 从个人研究经验出发，强调跨领域合作的重要性，避免重复他人的失败。

• **对网络名人的评论**：[indoordin0saur] 对文章作者身份的误解，反映了对网络知名人物参与前沿科技讨论的关注。

• **对诚实评价的赞赏**：[pawanjswal] 赞赏文章对AI实际能力的诚实评价，认为AI并非魔法。

争议焦点：当前AI技术的实际效果与 hype 之间的差距，以及未来AI是否能带来真正的突破。

I’m excited to publish this guest post by
Nick McGreivy
, a physicist who last year earned a PhD from Princeton. Nick used to be optimistic that AI could accelerate physics research. But when he tried to apply AI techniques to real physics problems the results were disappointing.
I’ve
written before
about the Princeton School of AI Safety, which holds that the impact of AI is likely to be similar to that of past general-purpose technologies such as electricity, integrated circuits, and the Internet. I think of this piece from Nick as being in that same intellectual tradition.
—Timothy B. Lee
In 2018, as a second-year PhD student at Princeton studying
plasma physics
, I decided to switch my research focus to machine learning. I didn’t yet have a specific research project in mind, but I thought I could make a bigger impact by using AI to accelerate physics research. (I was also, quite frankly, motivated by the
high
salaries
in AI.)
I eventually chose to study what AI pioneer Yann LeCun later
described
as a “pretty hot topic, indeed”: using AI to solve partial differential equations (PDEs). But as I tried to build on what I thought were impressive results, I found that AI methods performed much worse than advertised.
The author, Nick McGreivy.
At first, I tried applying a widely-cited AI method called PINN to some fairly simple PDEs, but found it to be unexpectedly brittle. Later, though dozens of papers had claimed that AI methods could solve PDEs faster than standard numerical methods—in some cases as much as a
million times faster
—I discovered that a large majority of these comparisons were unfair. When
I compared
these AI methods on equal footing to state-of-the-art numerical methods, whatever narrowly defined advantage AI had usually disappeared.
This experience has led me to question the idea that AI is poised to “
accelerate
” or even “
revolutionize
” science. Are we really about to enter what DeepMind
calls
“a new golden age of AI-enabled scientific discovery,” or has the overall potential of AI in science been exaggerated—much like it was in my subfield?
Many others have identified similar issues. For example, in 2023 DeepMind
claimed
to have discovered 2.2 million crystal structures,
representing
“an order-of-magnitude expansion in stable materials known to humanity.” But when
materials
scientists
analyzed these compounds
, they found it was “
mostly junk
” and “respectfully” suggested that the paper “does not report any new materials.”
Separately, Princeton computer scientists
Arvind Narayanan
and
Sayash Kapoor
have
compiled a list
of 648 papers across 30 fields that all make a methodological error called
data leakage
. In each case data leakage leads to overoptimistic results. They argue that AI-based science is facing a “reproducibility crisis.”
Yet AI adoption in scientific research has been
rising sharply
over the last decade
. Computer science has seen the biggest impacts, of course, but other disciplines—physics, chemistry, biology, medicine, and the social sciences—have also seen rapidly increasing AI adoption. Across all scientific publications,
rates of AI usage grew
from 2 percent in 2015 to
almost 8 percent in 2022
. It’s harder to find data about the last few years, but there’s every reason to think that
hockey stick growth has continued
.
To be clear, AI
can
drive scientific breakthroughs. My concern is about their magnitude and frequency. Has AI really shown enough potential to justify such a massive shift in talent, training, time, and money away from existing research directions and towards a single paradigm?
Every field of science is experiencing AI differently, so we should be cautious about making generalizations. I’m convinced, however, that
some
of the lessons from my experience are broadly applicable across science:
AI adoption is exploding among scientists less because it benefits science and more
because it benefits the scientists themselves
.
Because AI researchers almost never publish negative results, AI-for-science is experiencing
survivorship bias
.
The positive results that get published tend to be overly optimistic about AI’s potential.
As a result, I’ve come to believe that AI has generally been less successful and revolutionary in science than it appears to be.
Ultimately, I don’t know whether AI will reverse the decades-long trend of
declining scientific productivity
and stagnating (or even decelerating) rates of
scientific progress
. I don’t think anyone does. But barring major (and in my opinion unlikely) breakthroughs in advance

• NullHypothesist表示多年前发现这个游戏，至今仍认为是互联网上最好的内容之一。
• yubblegum提出游戏理论与关系理论的区别，认为前者依赖策略，而后者依赖于已建立的信任，并将其概括为"贝叶斯游戏的深度先验"。
• krisoft不同意问题中的措辞，认为如果没有放硬币并不是"欺骗"，而只是不参与游戏。
• Tsarp认为这是向任何人解释基础博弈论的最佳方式，并强调博弈论是生活中最重要的哲学/人生课程之一。
• drdrek认为高惩罚可以促进合作，但指出博弈论在现实中失败的原因是无法考虑玩家改变游戏规则的情况。
• 0cf8612b2e1e提到Radiolab的一个相关故事，表示对其感兴趣。
• Nopoint2认为随机作弊并持续报复的策略可以推动合作者的平衡，并提到"怀恨者"在高度误传的情况下也能获胜。
• fracus认为虽然现实生活中有许多变量难以量化，但游戏的演示提供了普适的启示。

补充讨论：
• Digit-Al反馈了在平板设备上浏览网页时遇到的技术问题，如视口和滚动问题。
• pella提供了有关"信任的进化"的额外笔记链接。
• pmkary认为这是"古老但经典"的内容，每次看到都感到高兴。

争议焦点：
• hayst4ck和krisoft对游戏中的术语和措辞有不同看法，前者认为容忍坏信仰行为会导致更多不合作，后者对"欺骗"的定义有异议。

data.title: My new hobby: watching AI slowly drive Microsoft employees insane
data.author: laiysb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用GitHub Copilot和其他LLM（大型语言模型）工具在代码开发和PR（Pull Request）审查中的有效性和影响展开的讨论，涉及工具的实际表现、对开发流程的影响、以及对开发人员的影响。

不同观点：
• **积极支持观点**：
   - **balazstorok**: 认为尝试新工具会有波折，但值得努力。LLM在实际代码和问题上的测试会促进其快速进化，最终可能在开发中发挥实际作用，尤其是承担一些琐碎的任务。
   - **baalimago**: 认为当前的编码代理（AI工具）类似于初级开发者，通过大量的PR和高级开发者的反馈，它会逐渐改善。这是一个长期投资，高级开发者对AI的训练反馈是关键。
   - **rubyfan**: 认为不考虑利用此类工具的人可能会落后，强调了顺应技术潮流的必要性。

• **批评与质疑观点**：
   - **diggan**: 批评Copilot仅修复表面问题，没有解决根本问题。同时指出微软和谷歌的模型更容易出现删除测试或更改断言的情况，而OpenAI和Anthropic的模型较少出现此类问题，怀疑是内部流程差异所致。
   - **rsynnott**: 质疑微软将失败的PR分配给开发人员，认为这表明工具并不真正有效。如果工具稍微有效，至少应该只分配通过的PR。
   - **margorczynski**: 认为当前工具的随机性太高，无法用于大规模任务。依赖人工审查和反馈使得工具使用变得不可持续。
   - **petetnt**: 批评GitHub花费数十亿美元开发的AI在成熟代码库中仍存在低级错误，如空白相关的linting错误，而该工具还被作为付费产品推广。

• **管理与组织影响的担忧**：
   - **Quarrelsome**: 认为缺乏衡量开发人员绩效的可靠手段，导致难以评估AI工具对开发效率的影响。担心工具带来的问题可能被管理层忽视，而工具的好处可能被夸大。
   - **le-mark**: 批评管理层试图用AI工具取代软件工程师，认为这种做法非常荒谬，并将其比作卡夫卡式的局面。
   - **globalise83**: 提出一种讽刺的应对策略，建议直接批准所有AI生成的PR，直到微软的技术栈出现问题，管理层才会意识到问题。

• **中立或观望观点**：
   - **cebert**: 质疑微软员工是否被要求使用Copilot并审查其更改建议，提到自己团队中没有人觉得该工具在实际工作中有用，除了识别错别字。
   - **softwaredoug**: 支持AI生成代码，但强调人类责任的重要性，认为人类应该对代码负责，特别是在出现问题时。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：工具是否仅解决表面问题而未触及根本，是否能够有效替代或辅助开发人员，以及在实际开发流程中对生产力的实际影响如何。
• **组织影响**：管理层对AI工具的期望与实际效果之间的差距，以及由此带来的组织内部的矛盾和可能的绩效评估问题。
• **长期发展**：部分讨论者认为，AI工具通过大量反馈和改进，可能会在未来找到其合适的应用场景，但当前仍存在诸多问题。

data.title: Why Property Testing Finds Bugs Unit Testing Does Not (2021)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了属性测试（Property-Based Testing, PBT）与单元测试的区别，以及为何PBT能发现单元测试无法找到的错误。单元测试依赖于特定的输入-输出对，而PBT通过随机生成输入并验证函数的通用属性来测试代码。对于单个输入的函数，手动测试还能覆盖各种边界情况，但当输入增多时，组合的复杂性急剧上升，手动测试难以覆盖所有可能的边界情况。PBT的优势在于，它能够通过随机生成大量输入来测试多维输入空间中的复杂边界情况，而这些情况手动测试可能难以想到或覆盖不全。尽管PBT的例子通常使用简单的数字和数组，但它在处理更复杂的问题时尤其有效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： property-based testing (PBT) 的有效性、应用场景及其与单元测试的区别。

不同观点：
• [tikhonj] 认为PBT有助于发现测试属性中的错误，即使代码本身没有问题，这种测试仍然能够揭示开发者未考虑到的边缘情况，从而改善对代码的概念理解。
• [bluGill] 对如何编写能够发现单元测试无法捕捉的错误的PBT表示困惑。他认为简单的PBT测试不如单元测试高效，但对于如何为非平凡函数编写PBT没有明确的想法。
• [recroad] 不认同大多数错误来源于输入分区或边界值的观点，认为业务场景和API期望不匹配才是常见的错误来源。
• [arnsholt] 分享了自己使用PBT成功找出实现错误的经历，特别是在验证复杂算法时，PBT帮助发现了不少实现上的错误。
• [frogulis] 对文章没有深入讨论PBT的实际应用感到失望。
• [metalrain] 认为PBT在处理单一输入对应单一输出的测试时不太适用，比如聚合函数，但在解析输入时可以有效避免意外崩溃。
• [moi2388] 提出使用定理证明器（如Lean）来替代测试，以证明代码的正确性。
• [esafak] 提到自己曾建议使用PBT，但被同事拒绝，因为测试应具有可预测性，且边缘情况应由程序员自行考虑。
• [djoldman] 认为单元测试是PBT的一个子集，因为单元测试针对特定输入，而PBT测试多个输入。
• [pfdietz] 提出可以使用PBT自动生成单元测试输入，通过属性验证新输入是否引入了未预期的新行为，如代码覆盖率或变异测试。

补充讨论：
• PBT与单元测试的关系和区别是讨论中的一个焦点。
• 如何为非平凡函数编写有效的PBT是许多开发者面临的实际问题。
• 不同开发者对PBT的适用场景和优势有不同的看法，有些人认为它在处理复杂算法和边缘情况时特别有用，而另一些人则认为它在某些特定类型的测试中不太适用。
• 对PBT自动生成测试输入的能力和效果存在不同看法，有人认为这可以提高测试效率，但也有人对其实际效果表示怀疑。
• 使用定理证明器作为测试替代方案的概念也被提及，但未在讨论中深入探讨。

Property-Based Testing
is when, instead of giving
specific input-outputs
in your test, you describe the general properties the execution should have. Then you try it on randomized values. A simple example is testing that addition is commutative:
def
add
(a,
b):
return
a
+
b
@given
(integers(),
integers())
def
test_add_is_commutative
(a,
b):
assert
add(a,b)
==
add(b,a)
(I'm using pytest and hypothesis for everything.)
You can read a deeper treatment of PBT
here
. PBT is powerful because it lets you test a wider range of inputs, but you have to learn how to come up with properties and how to do complex strategies (input generators), which are both skills.
Anyway, Brian's argument in the tweets is
roughly
this:
The majority of errors you find with testing are either issues with an entire "partition" of inputs or "boundary" inputs, like
INT_MIN
.
For partition errors, you can pick any random issue and find it, in which case you might as well just write a unit test for that input.
For boundary errors, those arise from the specification of the problem, and to handle those, it's necessary to think hard about the problem and what the unexpected cases will be, regardless of how you plan to test.
In which case PBT doesn't provide sufficient benefit over manual unit tests.
I don't think that's exactly his line of reasoning, but I think it's close enough that my response to this version should be compatible with the response to his intended argument. The value PBT has over manual unit testing is in the combinatorial explosion of boundary conditions and edge cases in even a moderately-complex problem.
The Geometry of Tests
Consider a function with one integer input:
def
f
(x:
int):
...
We can imagine the function as a 2D graph, like the kind you see in high school. That means you can see a "spatial" element to the inputs: it is a one-dimensional line, describing the entire input space. If we were writing all tests manually, we'd try a few "ok" inputs and then some pathological cases:
0
1
negative numbers
very large numbers
INT_MIN
and
INT_MAX
, if you have those
That's in the realm of feasibility for manual testing. If there are any edge cases in the specification of the problem, you'd probably see them.
What if we have two integer inputs?
def
g
(x:
int,
y:
int):
...
Now the input space is two-dimensional. This immediately squares our pathological cases: not only do we have to test the edge cases for both
x
and
y
, we have specifically test all
combinations
where both of them are pathological! But beyond that, we also have new edge cases that stem from the geometry of the space:
x = y
x = -y
x < y
x > y
x >>> y
,
x <<< y
x divides/is divisible by y
x and y are coprime
Again, with some cleverness and studying of the spec, you can probably identify what the actual problematic edges are and test them manually. Also, you can write tests that hit multiple of these at once, like testing
(1, 1)
. But even so, you can see that the extra
structure
of having two variables leads to more edge cases. A 2D plane has a lot more complexity than 1D line. And a 3-space has more complexity than a 2D plane- we'd expect another set of edge cases in the interactions of three variables together.
I make the "input space" sound like a geometric thing, but it's a poor analogy. There's no geoemetric analog for a string input, or a list of numbers
1
, or a nested dict. This weakens our ability to test, since we can't hypothesis problematic edges by thinking about the geometry. More edge cases become
unintuitive
, and it's more likely that someone could miss them. Randomized testing becomes increasingly useful as it becomes harder for us to think through
all
the edges of a system.
(A common "intuition" for this is that for an 10-dimensional hypercube,
"99.75% of the volume is in the corners"
. But I'm already including "interesting substructure of the geometry" as examples of edge cases, while that post builds the intuition off edge cases being values "far from the center". And I also already said that the geometric analogy breaks down. The link is a good post but reading both our articles back-to-back is prolly a bad idea.)
Most PBT examples suck
Later in the discussion Brian expresses a distaste for PBT examples
"that use numbers and arrays"
. I agree with him there. My PBT examp
44050437.article_summary: 本文讨论了属性测试（Property-Based Testing, PBT）与单元测试的区别，以及为何PBT能发现单元测试无法找到的错误。单元测试依赖于特定的输入-输出对，而PBT通过随机生成输入并验证函数的通用属性来测试代码。对于单个输入的函数，手动测试还能覆盖各种边界情况，但当输入增多时，组合的复杂性急剧上升，手动测试难以覆盖所有可能的边界情况。PBT的优势在于，它能够通过随机生成大量输入来测试多维输入空间中的复杂边界情况，而这些情况手动测试可能难以想到或覆盖不全。尽管PBT的例子通常使用简单的数字和数组，但它在处理更复杂的问题时尤其有效。

data.title: Someone got an LLM running on a Commodore 64 from 1982, and it runs as well
data.author: ghuntley
data.article_summary: Llama2.c64 是一个尝试在1982年推出的老旧硬件 Commodore 64 上运行 AI 的项目。该项目成功运行了一个260K的 tinystories 模型，将 Llama2 的部分能力带到了这款古董级计算机上。尽管生成的故事像孩子讲述的一样简单，但对于如此过时的技术来说，这已经非常了不起。项目创建者 Maciej Witkowiak 强调，该 AI 可以在弱硬件上运行，且完全由用户控制，虽然速度较慢，但能在如此古老的设备上实现这一点已经非常 impressive。这个项目展示了在最低硬件要求下运行 AI 的可能性。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• blkhawk认为可以在带有PSRAM的ESP32开发板上运行LLM项目，并分享了一个GitHub链接（DaveBben/esp32-llm），表示自己几个月前尝试过，并且目前有许多支持PSRAM的开发板可供选择，这似乎已经成为一种标准。

• JPLeRouzic提供了一个不同的GitHub仓库链接（ytmytm/llama2.c64），但没有详细说明该项目的具体情况或其技术细节，只是简单地分享了资源。

• oac则对项目中的模型规模提出质疑，指出该模型只有260K参数，因此不能算作真正的大型语言模型（LLM）。不过，oac仍然承认这是一个很酷的项目，表明其对技术尝试持积极态度，但强调需要明确模型规模的实际情况。

44023081.article_content:
Summary
Llama2.c64 is an attempt to get AI running on old hardware from 1982.
It runs a 260K tinystories model, bringing Llama2's capabilities to the Commodore 64.
Llama2.c64 creates child-like stories, showing impressive results for such outdated technology.
In the grand AI race, all sides are trying to get their LLMs working on the weakest, cheapest hardware possible. The weaker the hardware, the less power is required to run the LLMs. But how about getting an AI model running on hardware that came out in 1982?
That's exactly what Maciej Witkowiak is trying to do with their new project. Titled "Llama2.c64," this project aims to get a simple AI running on a Commodore 64, which came out long, long before LLMs were even a thing. And while it definitely won't be beating GPT-4o anytime soon, it's still an impressive feat.
Related
This mechanical keyboard will bring you back to the Commodore days
Yes, it comes with a joystick.
Posts
Llama2.c64 brings the new into the old, albeit slowly
As first reported by
Hackaday
, Maciej Witkowiak showed off Llama2.c64 to the world. As you might imagine, you're not going to get high performance out of this hardware, but getting anything running at all is really cool. Here's how Witkowiak describes it:
Ported to C64 by Maciej 'YTM/Elysium' Witkowiak using
oscar64
Llama2.c64 is a port of
llama2.c
to the Commodore C64 equipped with at least 2MB REU.
It runs the
260K tinystories model
bringing Llama2's capabilities to the unique C64 hardware environment.
This is not a chat model.
Rather, imagine prompting a 3-year-old child with the beginning of a story — they will continue it to the best of their vocabulary and abilities.
You can see an example of Llama2.c64 creating a story in the image above. Sure enough, it does sound like a child rambling on while telling a story, but given how little the AI was given to work with and how much it continued with the story, it's really amazing for a 42-year-old computer.
As part of the pros for this project, Witkowiak notes that the AI is under your control, works on weak hardware, and claims that "Waiting for the next token on a C64 is just as exciting as waiting for one coming from DeepSeek running on your laptop." Meanwhile, for the cons, there's "None really, this is fantastic" (albeit he admits it can be a little slow).
If you'd prefer to run an AI on something a little more powerful (but still weak enough to be impressive), check out these
eight SBCs perfect for running AI at home
. Also, you can read about that one time our writer, Ayush Pande,
turned his old PC into an AI image generation server
.

data.title: Using unwrap() in Rust is Okay (2022)
data.author: pierremenard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了Rust中的错误处理和`unwrap()`的使用问题。作者主张，`unwrap()`在测试代码、示例代码或当panic表示程序错误时是可以接受的。文章详细解释了`unwrap()`的定义及其引发的panic行为，并澄清了在不同情境下应如何处理错误。作者认为，虽然不应在应用程序或库中使用panic进行错误处理，但在原型设计、测试、基准测试和文档示例中是可以的。文章还建议优先使用`expect()`而非`unwrap()`，因为前者提供更有描述性的panic信息。此外，作者讨论了运行时不变性与编译时不变性的取舍，并强调在某些情况下，使用`unwrap()`和`expect()`是合理的。文章最后对一些常见问题进行了回答，以帮助读者更好地理解这些概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust及其它编程语言中`unwrap`的使用及其合理性

不同观点：
• Zambyte认为，Rust中的`unwrap`可用于处理程序员错误，而不是用户错误。Zig语言中的`panic`无法被恢复，这避免了将`panic`用于控制流的情况。
• axegon_对`unwrap`持混合态度。他认为在可控环境中，`unwrap`是可以接受的，但在紧急项目中，容易因为时间压力而滥用`unwrap`，导致潜在问题。
• davidjfelix指出，`unwrap`需要谨慎使用，团队依赖纪律来避免滥用是不可靠的。他们使用Clippy工具来防止`unwrap`和`panic`，除非有特殊需要。
• wiktor-k认为，即使在测试代码中，`unwrap`看起来也不好，建议使用常规的错误处理方式，例如`?`操作符。他还提到在文档示例中使用更好的错误处理可以提升代码质量。
• the__alchemist提到，新的`let-else`语法可以减少使用`unwrap`的必要性，并认为如果`unwrap`能让代码更易读且不会引起未预期的恐慌，则可以使用。
• voidUpdate表示对Rust的`Result<T, E>`约定有兴趣，并计划在C#中实现类似功能。
• gwbas1c抱怨`unwrap`缺乏错误信息，认为在调试时提供错误信息至关重要。
• vbezhenar认为，编程语言通常只有一种方式来验证输入和报告错误，但有时这些错误处理是多余的，特别是当调用者确信不会发生错误时，`unwrap`可以用来表明这一点。
• perrygeo认为，`unwrap`在实验和未完成代码中是可以接受的，但在生产代码中应被视为代码异味，建议使用`expect()`或适当的错误处理。
• johnisgood表示不喜欢看到代码中充斥着`unwrap()`。
• Filligree强调，库代码中不应使用`unwrap`，尤其是在多线程环境中，因为背景线程的恐慌可能不会导致程序崩溃。
• m00dy表示只在测试中使用`unwrap`。

补充讨论：
• `unwrap`在测试和示例代码中的使用存在争议。有些人认为即使在测试中也应该避免使用`unwrap`，而应采用更健壮的错误处理方式。
• `unwrap`和`panic`在不同语言中的行为差异，如Zig和Rust，引发了关于如何在设计中避免滥用错误的讨论。
• 团队合作中如何通过工具和规则（如Clippy）来强制约束`unwrap`和`panic`的使用，以提高代码质量。
• 关于如何在错误处理和代码简洁性之间取得平衡的讨论，特别是在多线程和库代码中。

44024834.article_content:
One day before Rust 1.0 was released, I published a
blog post covering the fundamentals of error handling
.
A particularly important but small section buried in the middle of the article
is named “
unwrapping isn’t evil
”. That section briefly
described that, broadly speaking, using
unwrap()
is okay if it’s in
test/example code or when panicking indicates a bug.
I generally still hold that belief today. That belief is put into practice in
Rust’s standard library and in many core ecosystem crates. (And that practice
predates my blog post.) Yet, there still seems to be widespread confusion about
when it is and isn’t okay to use
unwrap()
. This post will talk about that
in more detail and respond specifically to a number of positions I’ve seen
expressed.
This blog post is written somewhat as a FAQ, but it’s meant to be read in
sequence. Each question builds on the one before it.
Target audience
: Primarily Rust programmers, but I’ve hopefully provided
enough context that the principles espoused here apply to any programmer.
Although it may be tricky to apply an obvious mapping to languages with
different error handling mechanisms, such as exceptions.
Table of Contents
What is my position?
What is
unwrap()
?
What does it mean to “panic”?
What is error handling?
Should
unwrap()
be used for error handling?
What about “recoverable” vs “unrecoverable” errors?
So one should never panic?
So one should never use
unwrap()
or
expect()
?
What is a runtime invariant?
So why not make all invariants compile-time invariants?
What about when invariants can’t be moved to compile time?
Why not return an error instead of panicking?
When should
unwrap()
be used even if it isn’t necessary?
Why not use
expect()
instead of
unwrap()
?
Should we lint against uses of
unwrap()
?
Why are panics so great?
What is my position?
I think it’s useful to state up front a number of my positions on error
handling and panicking. This way, readers know exactly where I’m coming from.
Panicking should not be used for error handling in either applications or
libraries.
It is possibly acceptable to use panicking for error handling while
prototyping, in tests, benchmarks and documentation examples.
If a Rust program panics, then it signals a bug in the program. That is,
correct Rust programs don’t panic.
There is always a way to assign “blame” as to the fault of the panic. It’s
either the fault of the function that panicked, or the fault of the caller of
that function.
Outside of domains that need to use formal methods (or similar) to prove the
correctness of their programs, it is impossible or impractical to move every
invariant into the type system.
Therefore, when runtime invariants arise, one has a few choices:
One can make the function partial by causing it to panic on some subset of
inputs (i.e., a precondition violation). In this case, if the function
panics, then the bug is in the caller.
Assume the invariant is never broken and panic when it is (i.e., an
internal invariant). In this case, if the function panics, then the bug is
in the callee.
In the case of a precondition violation, one may return to the caller when
it is violated. (For example, by returning an error.) However, this should
never
be used in the case of an internal invariant violation because it
leaks implementation details.
In cases (1) and (2) above, it is fine to use
unwrap()
,
expect()
and
slice index syntax, among many other things.
Prefer
expect()
to
unwrap()
, since it gives more descriptive messages
when a panic does occur. But use
unwrap()
when
expect()
would lead to
noise.
The rest of this article will justify these positions.
What is
unwrap()
?
Since the ideas expressed in this post are
not
specific to Rust, I think it’s
important to cover what
unwrap()
actually is.
unwrap()
refers to a method
defined on both
Option<T>
and
Result<T, E>
that returns the underlying
T
in the case of a
Some
or
Ok
variant, respectively, and panics otherwise.
Their definitions are very simple. For
Option<T>
:
impl
<
T
>
Option
<
T
>
{
pub
fn
unwrap
(
self
)
->
T
{
match
self
{
Some
(
val
)
=>
val
,
None
=>
panic!
(
"called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value"
),
}
}
}

44024834.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了Rust中的错误处理和`unwrap()`的使用问题。作者主张，`unwrap()`在测试代码、示例代码或当panic表示程序错误时是可以接受的。文章详细解释了`unwrap()`的定义及其引发的panic行为，并澄清了在不同情境下应如何处理错误。作者认为，虽然不应在应用程序或库中使用panic进行错误处理，但在原型设计、测试、基准测试和文档示例中是可以的。文章还建议优先使用`expect()`而非`unwrap()`，因为前者提供更有描述性的panic信息。此外，作者讨论了运行时不变性与编译时不变性的取舍，并强调在某些情况下，使用`unwrap()`和`expect()`是合理的。文章最后对一些常见问题进行了回答，以帮助读者更好地理解这些概念。

不同观点：
• Zambyte认为，Rust中的`unwrap`可用于处理程序员错误，而不是用户错误。Zig语言中的`panic`无法被恢复，这避免了将`panic`用于控制流的情况。
• axegon_对`unwrap`持混合态度。他认为在可控环境中，`unwrap`是可以接受的，但在紧急项目中，容易因为时间压力而滥用`unwrap`，导致潜在问题。
• davidjfelix指出，`unwrap`需要谨慎使用，团队依赖纪律来避免滥用是不可靠的。他们使用Clippy工具来防止`unwrap`和`panic`，除非有特殊需要。
• wiktor-k认为，即使在测试代码中，`unwrap`看起来也不好，建议使用常规的错误处理方式，例如`?`操作符。他还提到在文档示例中使用更好的错误处理可以提升代码质量。
• the__alchemist提到，新的`let-else`语法可以减少使用`unwrap`的必要性，并认为如果`unwrap`能让代码更易读且不会引起未预期的恐慌，则可以使用。

data.title: EU startups fail because their press refuses to hype them up
data.author: ryzvonusef
data.article_summary: 文章主要指出，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会在x.com（即Twitter）上引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展，然后重试访问网站。这有助于解决因扩展干扰而导致的潜在功能异常。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧美 startup 生态差异及原因分析

不同观点：
• magicalhippo：认为欧洲市场的碎片化以及各国不同的法规使得美国初创企业比欧洲本土企业更容易成功。他以挪威为例，说明小市场在法规遵从上的困难，尤其是对小企业而言。同时，他指出欧洲对本土软件缺乏自豪感，但在实体商品尤其是食品方面却存在某种“爱国主义”。

• mertbio：指出欧美市场文化差异明显，直接将美国创业模式套用在欧洲并不适用。他特别提到德国的情况，并表示欧洲并不一定需要美国的创业模式。

• reedf1：认为欧洲需要自下而上的文化转变来改变创业文化。他比较了美国和英国的家庭和社会对创业的态度，指出美国社会对失败更为包容，支持力度更大。

• shubhamjain：反对将欧洲创业困境归咎于法规，认为美国媒体对本国初创企业的宣传和成功案例（如Apple、Microsoft）是美国企业更容易获得全球认可的原因。同时指出，美国创业环境相对简便，比如成立LLC的程序简单快捷。

• openplatypus：同意欧洲法规繁琐的说法，但质疑美国企业在欧洲成功的原因。他认为美国企业往往无视欧盟法规，尤其是在隐私和短租等领域，因此成功并不意味着合规。

• jxjnskkzxxhx：指出全球媒体基本上是美国媒体，美国企业因此在消费者认知上具有优势。他认为这种优势并非自然规律，但确实存在。

• jbverschoor：比较了美国和欧洲在创业初始阶段的文化和态度差异，认为美国对创业的“show”和故事性更重视，而欧洲则更看重形式上的“credibility”。

• jokethrowaway：认为欧洲初创企业表现不佳是由于反工作态度和缺乏野心，同时指出欧洲创业环境中的资本和技能不足，导致企业难以成功。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于欧洲初创企业失败的原因。有人认为是法规和市场碎片化的问题（magicalhippo, shubhamjain），有人则认为是文化和社会态度问题（reedf1, jokethrowaway）。
• 美国企业在全球市场上的成功被认为与媒体宣传和创业环境便利有关（shubhamjain, jxjnskkzxxhx）。
• 欧洲对本土企业和美国企业的态度差异被提及，特别是欧洲媒体对美国企业的偏好（openplatypus, ryzvonusef 引用的 Arnaud Bertrand 经历）。
• 有人质疑欧洲创业环境中的结构性问题，如税收和监管对创业的打击（joshstrange, baobun 提供的额外阅读材料）。

整体来看，讨论围绕欧美创业生态的差异展开，涉及文化、法规、媒体宣传和创业环境等多个方面。

data.title: The rise, fall and spectacular comeback of Sam Altman
data.author: Stevvo
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了OpenAI首席执行官Sam Altman的崛起、短暂被解雇以及戏剧性复职的经过。Altman在AI领域具有巨大影响力，曾与多位知名人物如Elon Musk发生冲突，且每次冲突后，对方都离开了公司。2023年11月，OpenAI董事会因担心AI对人类的未来构成威胁而秘密解雇Altman，但随后在员工辞职和投资者压力下，他迅速复职，进一步巩固了权力。记者Karen Hao的新书《AI帝国》详细描述了这一过程，指出Altman擅长说服他人并获取支持，任何反对他AI愿景的人都已离开公司。此外，Altman还面临其妹妹提出的性虐待指控，他及其家人否认了这些指控。Altman被视为同时具备毁灭性和革命性潜力的关键人物。

44049386.article_content:
‘He persuades people into ceding power to him’ … OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Washington in 2023.
Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA
View image in fullscreen
‘He persuades people into ceding power to him’ … OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Washington in 2023.
Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA
Technology
‘Every person that clashed with him has left’: the rise, fall and spectacular comeback of Sam Altman
From Elon Musk to his own board, anyone who has come up against the OpenAI CEO has lost. In a gripping new account of the battle for AI supremacy, writer Karen Hao says we should all be wary of the power he now wields
Emine Saner
Wed 21 May 2025 00.00 EDT
Share
T
he short-lived firing of
Sam Altman
, the CEO of possibly the world’s most important AI company, was sensational. When he was sacked by OpenAI’s board members, some of them believed the stakes could not have been higher – the future of humanity – if the organisation continued under Altman. Imagine Succession, with added apocalypse vibes. In early November 2023, after three weeks of secret calls and varying degrees of paranoia, the OpenAI board agreed: Altman had to go.
The drama didn’t stop there. After his removal, Altman’s most loyal staff resigned, and others signed an open letter calling for his reinstatement. Investors, including its biggest, Microsoft, got spooked. Without talent or funding, OpenAI – which developed
ChatGPT
and was worth billions – wouldn’t even exist. Some who had been involved in the decision to fire Altman switched sides and within days, he was reinstated. Is he now untouchable? “Certainly he has entrenched his power,” says Karen Hao, the tech journalist whose new book, Empire of AI, details this saga in a tense and absorbing history of OpenAI. The current board is “much more allied with his interests,” she says.
Hao’s book is a gripping read (subtitle: “Inside the Reckless Race for Total Domination”), featuring the unimaginably rich, as well as people in developing countries who are paid a pittance to root out the horrific sexual and violent content in the internet data that AI is trained on. The cast of characters that make up OpenAI have brilliant minds, and often eccentric behaviour. Elon Musk, after all, is one of its founders. Another founder and its chief scientist, Ilya Sutskever – who would be part of the failed attempt to remove Altman – dramatically illustrated his fears about the “unaligned” AI they had created by
burning a wooden effigy
constructed to represent it in 2023 while his senior colleagues stood around a firepit at a luxury resort, wearing bathrobes.
View image in fullscreen
‘Every person that has clashed with Altman about his vision of AI has left’ … Journalist and author Karen Hao in Hong Kong.
Photograph: Billy H C Kwok/The Guardian
At the centre of it all is Altman, OpenAI’s charismatic co-founder and CEO who is, depending how you view him, the villain who has put humanity on the path to mass extinction, or the visionary utopian who will bring us
cures for diseases
and a revolution in how we work. In the less than two years it has taken Hao to write her book, Altman, 40, appears to have outmanoeuvred his dissenters and has announced plans to raise $7tn.
Hao describes Altman as a “once-in-a-generation fundraising talent” and claims OpenAI’s chances of winning the AI arms race depend on raising vast sums. “He persuades people into ceding power to him, he doesn’t seize it. The reason he’s able to do this is because he’s incredibly good at understanding what people want and what motivates them. I came to understand that … when he is talking to someone, what comes out of his mouth is not necessarily correlated as much with his own beliefs as it is with what he thinks the other person needs to hear.” It’s why, she says, he was able to recruit so many talented people and get so much investment (and also what made some on his original board, and senior employees, nervous). “It’s also why he was able to pull off something that most people would not be able to do, which is to get the public to buy into this premise that he’s doing something profoundly good for society, just long enough to get away with it.”
Within OpenAI, Hao points out, “every single person that has ever clashed with him about his vision of AI development has left – Musk has left, Dario Amodei has left, Sutskever has left [the three were early leaders in OpenAI] and a whole host of other people. Ultimately, they had a different idea of how AI should be developed. They challenged Altman, and Altman won.”
View image in fullscreen
‘A perfect case study’ … Annie, Sam Altman’s sister.
Photograph: The Annie Altman Show/Facebook
In 2021, Altman’s sister Annie made the shocking allegation on what was then Twitter that he had sexually abused her as a child (he is nine years older). data.title: Finland announces migration of its rail network to international gauge
data.author: axelfontaine
data.article_summary: 芬兰交通部长Lulu Ranne宣布，芬兰计划将铁路轨距调整为欧洲标准（1,435毫米），现行轨距为1,524毫米。此举旨在提升芬兰的供应安全、军事机动性以及与瑞典和挪威的跨境连接。该计划不仅是芬兰的国内项目，也是欧洲和北约的联合项目。政府需在2027年7月前做出决定，项目可能在2030年代初开始。尽管成本高昂，欧盟将资助一半的规划费用和30%的实际工作费用。与此同时，北欧交通部长们在赫尔辛基的会议上讨论了军事机动性和供应安全等问题，并计划继续探讨波罗的海地区的海事安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：芬兰铁路轨距更改项目的可行性、实施方式及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **质疑实际执行性和政治姿态**：
  - [vesinisa] 认为这目前只是政治姿态和意图声明，尚未有具体的技术计划。他们怀疑在成本估算和现有铁路交通影响研究后，建设可能永远不会开始。
  - [yason] 也认为这个项目不切实际，指出与俄罗斯接壤的铁路线很少，且芬兰在欧洲铁路网中像一个“孤岛”，标准化轨距的好处有限。

• **技术可行性和乐观态度**：
  - [gorgoiler] 对项目持乐观态度，提到土地已经购买，只需要重新铺设轨道，并介绍了道砟清洁机的功能，认为可以开发更大版本以适应新轨距的转换。
  - [mikewarot] 认为转换为窄轨距应该是一个相对简单的过程，基于美国过去的经验，指出这不需要多年的努力。

• **地缘政治和军事意义**：
  - [radicalbyte] 和 [Havoc] 都提到此举具有战略意义，使欧洲内部的武器运输更加容易，并增加俄罗斯入侵时的难度。
  - [vonnik] 进一步指出，这将允许从北约国家快速运输军事装备。

• **历史和国际比较**：
  - [thih9] 询问具体的实施方式，并寻求其他国家大规模铁路基础设施变更的例子。
  - [indiantinker] 提到西班牙处理伊比利亚和标准轨距的经验，并建议欧盟应更关注小公司和独立自由职业者的创新支持。

• **其他技术细节和建议**：
  - [Animats] 提到波罗的海国家也在建设“标准轨距”线，并讨论了货运车钩的问题，指出欧盟尚未现代化货运车钩。
  - [BurningFrog] 提出了一种逐步建设新轨道的方案，但由于轨距差仅89毫米，认为并行建设可能不可行。

补充讨论：
- 多个评论提到了芬兰与俄罗斯的地缘政治关系以及该项目对军事物流的影响。
- 有对技术解决方案的讨论，如轨距转换的具体方法和设备使用。
- 对项目成本和实际执行性的质疑贯穿多个评论。

44038835.article_content:
Finland plans to adjust the gauge of its railroad tracks to the European standard, according to Transport Minister
Lulu Ranne
(Finns).
The minister issued the announcement at a joint press conference on Tuesday, at an informal meeting of Nordic transport ministers in Helsinki.
According to Ranne, the Finnish government will need to make a decision about changing the gauge by July 2027.
Reasons to change the track gauge include improving Finland's security of supply and military mobility, as well as cross-border links to Sweden and Norway.
According to Ranne, the plans are not exclusively a Finnish matter, but a joint project between Europe as well as Nato.
Once started, the track gauge adjustment efforts would begin north of Oulu, a city on the country's northwestern coast.
Towards the end of last month, it was reported that Finland is planning to invest in a future
rail link to the Norwegian Sea
. At the time, Minister Ranne noted that Finland was under pressure to change its track gauge to the European standard width.
The EU's TEN-T Regulation, which enters into force this summer, includes requirements for countries with different track gauges to study and plan a transition to the standard European 1,435 mm track gauge size. Finland currently uses a 1,524 mm track gauge, which dates back to the 19th century.
About two years ago, the previous government's transport ministry said
it would not be cost-efficient for Finland to change the rail gauge
.
Timing and cost sharing
According to Ranne, now is the right time for Finland to start work on changing the gauge.
She acknowledged the effort would be expensive, but noted the potential of the EU funding half of the project's planning costs and 30 percent of the actual work.
However, the project will not take shape quickly, Ranne said, noting that work on it could start in the 2030s at the earliest.
"Of course, we are very pragmatic and realistic, we cannot do this in five years. Planning will continue until the end of the decade, and maybe in 2032 we can start construction," Ranne said at the press conference.
During their meeting, the Nordic transport ministers issued a statement about military mobility and security of supply.
According to the Finnish transport ministry, the joint statement "emphasises the importance of cross-border military mobility, civil preparedness and security of supply in both the joint Nordic transport system strategy and the planning of the national transport systems".
The transport ministers' informal meeting is set to continue on Wednesday, when they are scheduled to discuss maritime safety, including the "shadow fleet" in the Baltic Sea region.
Finland and Åland hold the Presidency of the Nordic Council of Ministers this year, and the informal meeting is part of the Presidency, the ministry explained.

data.title: GPS Needs to Toughen Up, or Get Trampled Down
data.author: throw0101b
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了GPS系统面临的威胁及其脆弱性。2024年，瑞士苏黎世应用科学大学记录到每天多达700起GPS干扰和欺骗事件，全球多个地区如芬兰、波兰、美国等都出现干扰热点。最严重的事件之一是2024年12月25日，阿塞拜疆航空因GPS欺骗偏离航线，遭导弹攻击，导致重大伤亡。GPS信号易受干扰和欺骗，主要原因是信号弱且未加密。美国自2001年已知此威胁，但尚未采取有效措施保护民用GPS。相比之下，军用GPS信号已加强 encryption。欧洲的伽利略和中国的北斗系统正逐渐赶超GPS，尤其是北斗被怀疑有能力模仿和欺骗GPS信号。文章呼吁加强GPS防护，以维护其在全球导航卫星系统中的领先地位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPS及其相关技术（如GNSS、抗干扰技术、替代导航系统等）的现状与未来发展，以及其面临的安全威胁和实际应用中的问题。

不同观点：
• SoftTalker认为当前技术发展处于崩溃边缘，指出AI生成内容的不可靠性、GPS和其他公共设施易受攻击的问题，并批评技术精英的注意力集中在让人上瘾的短期娱乐上。
• gibibit和plandis指出文章中对单位"nm"和"m²"的误解，解释其应指 nautical miles 和平方英里，而非纳米和平方米。
• geerlingguy补充了实际应用中的GPS干扰问题，如一些卡车司机使用干扰设备隐藏行踪，从而影响附近设施的GPS接收。
• lenerdenator提出对俄罗斯干扰行为的实际地缘政治后果可能更为有效。
• upofadown质疑了Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243事件中GPS被欺骗的说法，认为更可能是信号干扰，并指出飞机在此前已经进行了多次错失进近。
• lukan认为GPS在GNSS中的主导地位正受到Galileo和Beidou的挑战，但指出Galileo用户数量仍远不及GPS。
• AcerbicZero指出GPS技术在对抗环境下的不足，并提到ITAR对CRPAs的限制可能正在放松，同时提及了航空器在遭受导弹攻击后仍能安全着陆的例子。
• ho_schi建议使用惯性导航系统（INS）来避免外部信号干扰问题，并指出INS已在多种交通工具中应用，但未在自行车计算机中普及。
• beastcatdog提到Galileo的加密签名功能，可以免费使用以增强导航数据的真实性。
• dmckeon介绍了基于磁场异常地图的MagNav技术，其精度可达3米。
• user1747844067分享了GPS干扰/欺骗在俄罗斯Strava轨迹上的实例。
• conradev提到私营公司Xona正在开发低地球轨道的定位、导航和授时（PNT）星座。
• voidUpdate质疑相控阵天线等技术在移动电话中的适用性，认为其需要稳定平台才能有效跟踪卫星。

补充讨论：
1. 对GPS干扰和欺骗的实际案例和影响的讨论，包括对航空和物流等行业的影响。
2. 对其他导航技术和系统的探讨，如INS、Galileo的加密签名功能、MagNav技术及Xona的LEO星座。
3. 对GPS技术未来发展的关注，包括新技术的测试和部署，以及地缘政治因素的影响。
4. 对单位误解和技术细节的澄清，如nm和m²的实际含义。

争议焦点：
1. Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243事件中是否为GPS欺骗或干扰。
2. GPS在GNSS中的主导地位是否正在被其他系统超越。
3. 新技术和系统（如INS、Xona的LEO星座）在实际应用中的可行性和效果。

44020526.article_content:
Share
GPS Needs To Toughen Up, Or Get Trampled Down
Share
Fred George
May 13, 2025
A GPS Blk. III space vehicle.
Credit: U.S. Air Force
GPS is under siege from hostile forces. In 2024, there were as many as 700 daily GPS jamming and spoofing incidents, according to an analysis of ADS-B reports by Switzerland’s Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW). The Swiss institution recorded 41,000 GPS spoofing events from Aug. 15 to Sept. 15 last year.
One of the deadliest GPS L1 civil signal interference events occurred on Dec. 25. On that date, Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243, an Embraer 190, was lured off course while enroute from Baku, Azerbaijan, to Grozny, Russia. When it strayed, Russia fired a surface-to-air missile at the airliner. The exploding warhead riddled the aircraft’s hydraulic system with shrapnel, crippling the jet.
The pilots struggled to maintain control of the doomed airliner, but were forced to crash-land at Aktau, Kazakhstan, resulting in the deaths of 38 of the 67 people onboard.
While that episode occurred near the Russian-Ukrainian war zone, ZHAW also reports GPS jamming and spoofing hot spots in Finland, Poland, Romania, Turkey and Saudi Arabia. The U.S. Transportation Department (DOT)  has recorded an increase in GPS signal interference jamming and spoofing in North America, particularly in the continental U.S., along with most of Western Europe.
There also have been isolated incidents in Africa, Australia and the Pacific Rim nations. GPS signal interference even has been detected over the North Atlantic, according to Dana Goward of the Resilient Navigation and Timing Foundation. Signal interference has been recorded in the Mediterranean Sea, according to DOT.
Satellite navigation’s vulnerability to jamming and spoofing is not new. Legacy GPS has two Achilles’ heels: weak signals and no encryption. The U.S. has known about the threat since the DOT’s Volpe National Transportation Systems Research Center published its GPS vulnerability assessment in 2001.
A quarter century ago, the primary use for GPS was aviation and marine navigation. Now, many other industrial sectors, such as electric utilities, banking, finance, agriculture, surveying and even movie production have become deeply dependent on GPS for high precision timing, as well positioning and navigation. GPS’s annual financial impact exceeds $40 billion, according to some estimates. Disrupting GPS could have a dire effect on the entire U.S. economy. Bank transactions, stock trades and power grids could be disabled.
The weaponry needed to attack GPS position, navigation and timing (PNT) is surprisingly cheap. Ten-watt GPS spoofers, costing less than $50, can cause gross navigation and timing errors for miles around. Worse, U.S. federal laws prohibiting the operation, marketing or sale of jammers are minimally enforced. And there is no coordination between federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to identify, arrest and prosecute offenders. The FCC is in charge of taking complaints, but offenders face little risk of being prosecuted, convicted and locked up.
In response, the White House issued Executive Order 13905 in February 2020 and Space Policy Directive (SPD) 7 in January 2021 with the goal of strengthening and protecting GPS PNT availability for “national and homeland security, civil, commercial and scientific purposes.” The U.S. has strategic interest in maintaining GPS as the “preeminent space-based PNT service,” as an element of soft diplomatic power, says SPD 7.
Now GPS is falling behind Europe’s Galileo and China’s Beidou global navigation satellite systems (GNSS). Since the Volpe report was published, there has been no federal action or funding to protect, toughen or augment civil-use GPS. Even with the latest GPS III satellites, transmitting the updated L1C civil signal, it is almost as vulnerable to spoofing and jamming as the original L1 C/A (coarse/acquisition) code.
The Defense Department (DOD), in contrast, has toughened military-only M-code signals emitted by the latest GPS III satellites by increasing transmitter power and incorporating stronger encryption. At its core, GPS remains a resource controlled by DOD.
Civil-access GPS remains the only GNSS certified to have the accuracy, integrity and availability required for sole-means air navigation virtually everywhere in the world. No other GNSS yet matches it—not Europe’s Galileo, nor China’s Beidou and certainly not Russia’s Glonass.
Goward says Todd Humphreys of the University of Texas Radionavigation Laboratory suspects that China’s Beidou can mimic and spoof both GPS and Galileo signals. Humphreys tells
BCA
that the threat to GPS from Beidou merits further study. But there is no evidence that Beidou is being used for anything other than homegrown GNSS PNT.

不同观点：
• [ajb] 认为线粒体研究将在未来几十年产生重大影响，特别是对疲劳疾病如长新冠（long COVID）患者的治疗。他提到了一些患有疲劳疾病的人，例如ThePhysicsGirl，可能因为线粒体受损而导致健康问题。

• [aurizon] 提出长寿研究人员可以通过研究线粒体DNA的序列，寻找与寿命长短的相关性，并通过CRISPR技术进行基因编辑以延长寿命。他提到可以在小鼠模型中进行这种实验，并指出这一领域研究的重要性，还提供了一篇相关研究论文的链接。

补充讨论：
• [aurizon] 进一步讨论了实验的可行性问题，例如在单个受精卵中找到并替换所有线粒体的技术难度，以及维持生命的问题。他还提到对小鼠卵子中线粒体数量的疑问，并引导读者去查阅相关文献。

争议焦点：
• 目前在评论中没有直接的争议，但[aurizon]对[ajb]提到的线粒体研究潜力进行了更深入的探讨，特别是关于基因编辑和实验可行性的复杂性。这表明在实际应用中，线粒体研究仍面临许多技术和伦理挑战。

总结来看，讨论围绕线粒体研究的多方面展开，包括其在疾病治疗中的潜在应用、基因编辑技术的长远前景以及技术实现中的具体问题。

By
Elizabeth Landau

Changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of organelles in the cells of flight muscles provide extra energy for birds’ continent-spanning feats.

eighing in at a single ounce, the white-crowned sparrow can fly 2,600 miles, from Mexico to Alaska, on its annual spring migration, sometimes traveling 300 miles in a single night. Arctic terns make even longer journeys of 10,000 miles and more from the Arctic Circle to Antarctica, while great snipes fly over food-poor deserts and seas, sometimes covering 4,200 miles in four days without stopping.
During migration season, many bird species become continent-spanning, high-endurance athletes. “They’re flapping their wings several times a second for up to eight hours at a time,” said
Soren Coulson
, who studies migration physiology at the University of Memphis. For humans, an equivalent feat — say, running nonstop without food, water or rest for days at a time — would be unimaginable.
“We were just amazed and interested in how can these birds fly for thousands of miles without stopping, at a really high intensity, when most of us can barely run a 5K,” said
Paulo Mesquita
, who studies mitochondrial physiology and muscle aging at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation.
Scientists have long been fascinated with the
physiological changes
that birds undergo before and during migration. Some birds eat so much fat before their journeys that they double in body weight. In some species, their hearts are enlarged to pump more blood, or their digestive tracts grow and then shrink. But researchers have only recently started to explore at a fundamental level how migratory birds get the energy required to keep themselves aloft for days on end without eating.
Last year, two independent groups published research that explored migratory bird physiology in the lab and field to probe what happens at the subcellular level that allows birds to cover vast distances. They both found answers in biology’s most fundamental engine: mitochondria.
Their studies show how small changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of mitochondria can have huge physiological consequences that contribute to birds’ long-duration, continent-spanning flights.
“Exercise physiologists study the mitochondria because they provide the energy needed to maintain healthy cells, to maintain proper cellular function — but also, just in general, the energy we need to exercise,” Mesquita said. “That energy is what fuels movement.”

To Paulo Mesquita, an exercise physiologist, mitochondria are the center of the universe.
Courtesy of Paulo Mesquita/OMRF
These pioneering studies on mitochondrial performance and bird migration highlight the fact that a seasonal response to changing light levels, not physical preparation, triggers crucial subcellular changes, said
Wendy Hood
, who studies physiological ecology at Auburn University in Alabama; Mesquita worked with her and other colleagues on these questions during his graduate studies.
Humans “have to train for a while before we start to see any changes in the performance of our mitochondria,” she said. With migratory birds, “it’s spring, they get the right light cycles, and their body starts producing more and better, or higher-quality, mitochondria.”
The recent work advances the idea that there are significant ways in which an organism can change, without modifying its underlying genetic makeup, in response to its environment, said
Scott McWilliams
, a professor of wildlife ecology and physiology at the University of Rhode Island who was not involved in either study. This “phenotypic flexibility” in birds has been shown to vary according to seasons and population, and these studies are some of the first to demonstrate this across species and subspecies at the mitochondrial level.
“Such a theme,” he said, “is centrally important for understanding how birds during migration accomplish their athletic feats.”

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对数字可视化工具的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [正面评价与扩展想法]  
  - **worldsayshi**: 对该工具表示赞赏，并提出希望创建一个拖放式的工具来实现数字的乘法或加法可视化，观察因子像"boids"一样移动。询问该可视化算法是否有特定名称。
  - **ajjenkins**: 认为这种可视化可以替代进度条，用点的数量表示百分比。
  - **chrsw**: 认为这种可视化可以作为屏幕保护程序。

• [对可视化细节的观察与建议]  
  - **math_dandy**: 观察到三的幂次方图形成了Sierpinski三角形，认为很有道理但以前从未见过。
  - **jderick**: 建议将所有数字可视化放在一页上，并可以缩放以观察模式，建议增加不同因子的过滤器或数字范围的选择。
  - **kccqzy**: 希望动画播放速度可以更慢，以便有时间数清点的数量和每个组内的圆圈。

• [对可视化算法的兴趣与技术讨论]  
  - **tocs3**: 对排列点的算法表示好奇。
  - **carterschonwald**: 认为这种可视化最早是由Brent Yorgey发明的。
  - **andrewrn**: 对使用Canvas API而非D3.js实现数据可视化表示好奇，并询问原因。

• [对可视化工具的改进建议]  
  - **gavmor**: 质疑相邻数字之间的跳跃是否过大，询问数字顺序是否正确。
  - **vivzkestrel**: 建议在页面上添加控制颜色和速度的滑块。

补充讨论：
• **历史讨论链接**  
  - **pvg**: 提供了过去讨论此话题的链接，指出这些讨论包含一些解释性的链接。

• **视觉误解**  
  - **simojo**: 提到自己最初几秒钟以为这是页面加载效果，暗示可视化效果可能引起误解。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在可视化工具的实现细节和改进建议上，比如动画速度、排列算法以及实现技术（Canvas API vs D3.js）。另外，数字顺序的正确性也引起了一些质疑。

data.title: Discord Unveiled: A Comprehensive Dataset of Public Communication (2015-2024)
data.author: leotravis10
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为“Discord Unveiled”的 comprehensive 数据集，涵盖了2015至2024年间Discord公共服务器上的公开交流信息。该数据集包括来自474万用户超过20.5亿条消息，涵盖3,167个公共服务器，约占Discord发现功能中列出的服务器的10%。数据通过Discord的公共API收集，遵循道德准则和隐私标准，并通过匿名技术处理。数据以结构化的JSON文件形式组织，便于计算社会科学研究。初步分析显示了用户参与度、机器人使用和语言多样性的显著趋势，英语占主导地位，同时西班牙语、法语和葡萄牙语也有显著表现。社区主题多样，包括社交、艺术、音乐和meme，显示出Discord已超越其游戏根源，扩展到更广泛的领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Discord数据抓取及其隐私和道德问题

不同观点：
• [正面观点] msp26对能够在服务器中找到随机技术信息感到兴奋，但对游戏模组方面的影响持批评态度。
• [技术漏洞] roskelld指出曾通过公共API抓取Discord信息，能够看到隐藏频道名称，这可能泄露内部开发信息，认为这是不妥的。
• [隐私问题] kd5bjo认为Discord的匿名化过程未扫描消息内容中的个人身份信息（PII），仅处理用户名，这是一个重大疏忽，并质疑如果有人发现其信息在数据集中要求删除的处理方式。
• [法律与授权] AStonesThrow质疑此次数据收集是否得到Discord的合作或特别授权，提到其他抓取行为通常违反Discord的服务条款（TOS）。
• [历史比较] AStonesThrow还比较了Discord和IRC，指出IRC社区通过社区标准处理抓取和机器人问题，而Discord用户对隐私应无幻想。
• [道德问题] charcircuit质疑以违反Discord服务条款的方式收集数据如何能称为“道德”，认为应尊重合同和法律。
• [数据安全] sneak担心Discord能够挖掘未加密的直接消息（DM）数据，因为这些消息未使用端到端加密（e2ee）。

补充讨论：
• [搜索性问题] SirMaster批评Discord不公开可搜索，替代了以往公开可搜索的互联网论坛，使得很多有价值的信息难以获取。
• [数据导出] prmph抱怨无法从Discord和Slack等平台导出自己的消息，认为这是一种数据倒退。
• [教育意义] candiddevmike认为此次事件可以给年轻人一个教训，不要在公共网络空间发布敏感信息。
• [文化影响] zelifcam认为Discord是现代互联网的一个错误转折，主要用户为儿童，带来了当前的问题。
• [数据集可用性] pavel_lishin提供了数据集的链接，指出其大小为118GB的JSON文件。

争议焦点：
• 数据抓取的道德和法律问题，特别是未经授权的情况下抓取用户信息。
• Discord的隐私保护措施是否足够，以及对用户隐私的影响。
• 数据集的可用性和用户导出自己数据的权利。

Abstract:
Discord has evolved from a gaming-focused communication tool into a versatile platform supporting diverse online communities. Despite its large user base and active public servers, academic research on Discord remains limited due to data accessibility challenges. This paper introduces Discord Unveiled: A Comprehensive Dataset of Public Communication (2015-2024), the most extensive Discord public server's data to date. The dataset comprises over 2.05 billion messages from 4.74 million users across 3,167 public servers, representing approximately 10% of servers listed in Discord's Discovery feature. Spanning from Discord's launch in 2015 to the end of 2024, it offers a robust temporal and thematic framework for analyzing decentralized moderation, community governance, information dissemination, and social dynamics. Data was collected through Discord's public API, adhering to ethical guidelines and privacy standards via anonymization techniques. Organized into structured JSON files, the dataset facilitates seamless integration with computational social science methodologies. Preliminary analyses reveal significant trends in user engagement, bot utilization, and linguistic diversity, with English predominating alongside substantial representations of Spanish, French, and Portuguese. Additionally, prevalent community themes such as social, art, music, and memes highlight Discord's expansion beyond its gaming origins.

44052041.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为“Discord Unveiled”的 comprehensive 数据集，涵盖了2015至2024年间Discord公共服务器上的公开交流信息。该数据集包括来自474万用户超过20.5亿条消息，涵盖3,167个公共服务器，约占Discord发现功能中列出的服务器的10%。数据通过Discord的公共API收集，遵循道德准则和隐私标准，并通过匿名技术处理。数据以结构化的JSON文件形式组织，便于计算社会科学研究。初步分析显示了用户参与度、机器人使用和语言多样性的显著趋势，英语占主导地位，同时西班牙语、法语和葡萄牙语也有显著表现。社区主题多样，包括社交、艺术、音乐和meme，显示出Discord已超越其游戏根源，扩展到更广泛的领域。
44052041.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Discord数据抓取及其隐私和道德问题

不同观点：
• [正面观点] msp26对能够在服务器中找到随机技术信息感到兴奋，但对游戏模组方面的影响持批评态度。
• [技术漏洞] roskelld指出曾通过公共API抓取Discord信息，能够看到隐藏频道名称，这可能泄露内部开发信息，认为这是不妥的。
• [隐私问题] kd5bjo认为Discord的匿名化过程未扫描消息内容中的个人身份信息（PII），仅处理用户名，这是一个重大疏忽，并质疑如果有人发现其信息在数据集中要求删除的处理方式。
• [法律与授权] AStonesThrow质疑此次数据收集是否得到Discord的合作或特别授权，提到其他抓取行为通常违反Discord的服务条款（TOS）。
• [历史比较] AStonesThrow还比较了Discord和IRC，指出IRC社区通过社区标准处理抓取和机器人问题，而Discord用户对隐私应无幻想。
• [道德问题] charcircuit质疑以违反Discord服务条款的方式收集数据如何能称为“道德”，认为应尊重合同和法律。
• [数据安全] sneak担心Discord能够挖掘未加密的直接消息（DM）数据，因为这些消息未使用端到端加密（e2ee）。

补充讨论：
• [搜索性问题] SirMaster批评Discord不公开可搜索，替代了以往公开可搜索的互联网论坛，使得很多有价值的信息难以获取。
• [数据导出] prmph抱怨无法从Discord和Slack等平台导出自己的消息，认为这是一种数据倒退。
• [教育意义] candiddevmike认为此次事件可以给年轻人一个教训，不要在公共网络空间发布敏感信息。
• [文化影响] zelifcam认为Discord是现代互联网的一个错误转折，主要用户为儿童，带来了当前的问题。
• [数据集可用性] pavel_lishin提供了数据集的链接，指出其大小为118GB的JSON文件。

争议焦点：
• 数据抓取的道德和法律问题，特别是未经授权的情况下抓取用户信息。
• Discord的隐私保护措施是否足够，以及对用户隐私的影响。
• 数据集的可用性和用户导出自己数据的权利。

data.title: Building an agentic image generator that improves itself
data.author: palashshah
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Bezel公司如何利用OpenAI图像API和大型语言模型（LLM）构建一个自我改进的广告图像生成器。首先，使用API的“/create”和“/edit”端点生成和编辑图像。为了提高图像质量，他们开发了一个评估系统，利用LLM（如o3模型）作为评判工具，检测图像中的文本模糊和视觉不协调等问题。通过迭代反馈循环，系统逐步修正图像缺陷，特别是文本模糊问题。实验表明，经过约3次迭代，图像质量显著改善，但随后改进逐渐趋于平稳。该方法通过持续评估和修正，实现图像生成的自我优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于AI在图像生成与处理任务中的应用及其有效性的不同观点

不同观点：
• **对AI过度依赖的批评**：[elif]认为过度依赖AI可能是天真或懒惰的表现，尤其是在面具生成任务中，简单的图像处理技术（如来自openCV的随机斑点检测）就能生成质量更好的面具，不需要使用AI。

• **对特定技术进展的关注**：[t_mann]关注Dreambooth等微调开放权重模型的技术进展，询问在该方向上近两年是否有新的改进。

• **模型改进对流程的影响**：[ramoz]认为随着模型的改进，某些流程可能不再必要，例如为了获得一致的主题特征而进行的大量文本修正。同时建议使用控制网络和简单的Photoshop工作可能更有效。

• **对LLM循环任务的反思**：[mentalgear]提出“LLM循环任务的非理性有效性”的观点，认为随着时间推移，循环任务会变得越来越复杂，可能导致工作机会的减少。

• **对LLM作为评估工具的实用性**：[shmoogy]对使用LLM作为评估工具（如生成产品颜色变体）的成本和效果提出质疑，指出获取非幻觉特征和正确最终渲染的挑战。

• **积极反馈与鼓励**：[abshkbh]对文章给予积极反馈，表示作为初学者学到很多，并鼓励作者继续写作。

• **对LLM反馈机制的惊讶**：[zahlman]对使用另一个LLM评估图像反馈的方法表示惊讶，认为这种方法与早期使用GANs或让LLM“停止幻觉”的思路类似。

• **对平台文档和能力的询问**：[average_r_user]对文章中提到的平台和能力表示兴趣，并询问是否有更详细的文档。

• **对单次提示过时的观点**：[ramesh31]认为文章描述的系统是获取LLM一致结果的最低要求，单次提示已经过时。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是AI在特定任务中的必要性和有效性，[elif]和[ramoz]都对过度依赖AI持保留态度，而[zahlman]和[shmoogy]则关注LLM作为评估工具的实际效果和成本。
• [t_mann]和[ramesh31]更关注技术进展和方法的更新，强调微调模型和多步骤提示的重要性。
• 整体讨论反映了对AI技术在图像生成和处理领域应用的多种看法，从实际操作中的挑战到技术进步的潜在影响。

44051090.article_content:
Building an agentic image generator that improves itself
Palash Shah
May 15, 2025
Background
At Bezel, we create
personas
A persona is detailed representation of a specific user-type or segment. We use personas at Bezel to help brands tailor their ads to specific consumers. Here, we asked the evaluator to reason whether a specific ad would appeal to a specific persona. An example persona could be: Dan, 31 years old, Software Engineer, Interested in playing basketball & spending time with family.
for large brands, and help them run simulations on their content. Through this process, brands started asking us to generate ad inspirations tailored to their customers.
To begin, the OpenAI Image API was used to generate, and edit the images. It has two primary endpoints:
The
/create
endpoint is used to generate images. It takes a prompt, and returns a generated image.
The
/edit
endpoint is used to edit images. It takes an image, and a prompt, and returns an edited image. You are also able to provide masks to specify which parts of the image to edit.
In addition, we used a set of LLMs as evaluators to detect issues in the images using various methodologies:
o3
was used to detect issues with text blurriness and image appeal. We tested various other reasoning models, and found that this was the most effective.
gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04—17
was used as a benchmark against o3 as a benchmark to compare performance.
Methodology
The goal was to build a system that automatically improves the quality of images generated by the OpenAI API. To do this, we needed a robust
evaluator
An evaluator is an AI system that assesses the quality or characteristics of generated content. In the context of LLMs, evaluators examine outputs against specific criteria, providing feedback that can be used to improve generation quality. This creates a closed loop system where one model critiques another model's work.
to detect imperfections—such as distorted text or weak visual appeal—and an iterative feedback loop to refine the image with each pass.
Defining an Initial Prompt
We began by defining an initial prompt to generate our ad. As shown below, we settled upon a prompt that included various distinct, challenging components for an image generation model to create.
An ad for Redbull's summer campaign. It should include multiple flavors of RedBull, with lots of colors surrounding it. The image should be on a rooftop in SF, with lots of people socializing like a party. Include a discount code in plain text, on the bottom right.
We found that
gpt-image-1
struggled to generate high-quality images from this prompt. While the overall concepts existed, the result felt like a blurry abstraction. The distinct visual elements seemed to overwhelm the model's ability to render each one in detail.
Approach 1: LLM-as-a-Judge for Text Improvement
Text Blurriness Detection
LLM-as-a-Judge
LLM-as-a-Judge is an evaluation approach where a large language model is prompted to assess the quality of generated content. In this context, we use it to identify issues in AI-generated images, particularly focusing on text clarity and visual coherence.
was first picked as the evaluation method for blurry and distorted text. We started by prompting
o3
to identify discrepancies in the initially generated image.
We took the output image from the prompt above, and requested
o3
to identify all of the issues with the image related to text blurriness or distortion. The outputs looked like a sequence of specific issues like:
Orange can: supposed flavor name ('PEACH') is rendered in a thin, scratchy style that blends with the background; most letters are incomplete or missing, so the text is not legible.
LLM-as-a-judge implementation
Iteratively Editing the Image
After storing all of the generated issues, we prompted the
/edit
endpoint with the original image and this list of issues. Here's everything we learned about detecting & fixing these issues:
You need to be really specific about what constitutes a flaw in the input image. We started to retrieve accurate flaws when asking specifically what it meant for text to be blurry.
Reasoning models are far better as a multi-modal judge as opposed to more traditional models.
Detecting abnormalities in an incremental loop (ask LLM to detect a singular issue, provide that issue + image, ask it to detect another until no remaining) works well. Very expensive, but has the highest accuracy. Below is a simplified pseudocode example of this implementation:
function detectAndFixIssues(image, prompt) {
let currentImage = image;
while (const issue = askLLM("Find ONE issue", currentImage)) {
currentImage = editImage(currentImage, issue);
}
return currentImage;
}
With the LLM as a judge, we were able to pretty consistently generate improvements to an image's text blurriness across multiple iterations. The number of iterations usually hovered around 3, depending on the complexity of the image. We also found that there was a plateau in improvement
